summaries.title: Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions
summaries.aiSummary: Rescinds 78 Biden Administration Executive Orders, including DEI initiatives, COVID precautions/relief, and the recent AI protections/study.

summaries.title: Memorandum to Resolve the Backlog of Security Clearances for Executive Office of the President Personnel
summaries.aiSummary: This Memo states that all personnel for the EOP shall immediately be granted interim Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearances for a period not to exceed 6 months and shall be immediately granted access to the facilities and technology necessary to perform duties.

summaries.title: Defending Women From Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government
summaries.aiSummary: This EO provides legal definitions for various "biological" gender terms that the agencies must adopt. The Secretary of HHS is directed to provide guidance expanding on the definitions listed in this order. The agencies are directed to adopt and reflect these terms in various manners, including in federal policies and documents, and submit an update on the implementation of this EO within 120 days.

summaries.title: Restoring Names That Honor American Greatness
summaries.aiSummary: Requires agencies to appoint members to the Board on Geographic Names. Reinstates the name "Mount McKinley" for the Denali Mountain. Renames the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America."

summaries.title: Protecting the Meaning and Value of American Citizenship
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that United States citizenship shall not extend to persons born in the United States when (1) the person's mother was unlawfully present in the United States and the person's father was not a United States citizen or lawful permanent resident at the time of the birth and (2) when the person's mother's presence in the United States was lawful but temporary and the person's father was not a United States citizen or lawful permanent resident at the time of the birth.

summaries.title: Protecting the United States From Foreign Terrorists and Other National Security and Public Safety Threats
summaries.aiSummary: The EO implements stricter vetting and screening processes for foreign nationals seeking entry. It also mandates collaboration between the Secretary of State, the AG, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the DNI to identify potential threats and ensure that immigrants do not harbor hostile intentions towards the U.S. The order also requires a review of current regulations to prevent the misuse of visa programs and ensure the proper assimilation of lawful immigrants. Additionally, it directs the evaluation of countries with deficient vetting information to determine the need for admission suspensions.

summaries.title: Declaring A National Emergency At The Southern Border Of The United States
summaries.aiSummary: This Memo declares that a national emergency exists at the southern border of the United States the requires the use of Armed Forces. The Memo directs the DoD to order as many units as appropriate to obtain complete control of the border. The Memo also directs DHS to construct physical barriers at the border and revokes the Biden Proclamation which redirecting funds for the border wall construction. The Memo also asks the DOT and FCC to consider waiving applicable regulations that restrict DHS's ability to use unmanned aerial systems.

summaries.title: Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid
summaries.aiSummary: Requires the applicable heads of departments and agencies to pause new awards of development assistance funds and prevent disbursement of funds under existing awards to foreign countries, non-governmental organizations, international organizations, and contractors pending review. Department of State will develop guidelines for review and departments/agencies will use guidelines to determine whether to continue, modify, or cease foreign assistance programs. Secretary of State may waive the pause for specific programs (no further information provided on waiver).

summaries.title: Protecting the American People Against Invasion
summaries.aiSummary: This EO sets forth several policies and procedures aimed at enforcing the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). The EO directs DHS and USCIS to prioritize enforcement of INA and other Federal laws related to illegal entry and unlawful presence of aliens in the United States. The EO directs the Attorney General to prioritize prosecution of criminal offenses related to the same. The EO aims to establish Homeland Security Task Forces in all states. The EO directs DHS to ensure the efficient and expedited removal of aliens from the United States and to construct detention facilities for aliens pending the outcome of their removal proceedings. The EO states that all "sanctuary jurisdictions" will no longer receive federal funds.

summaries.title: Guaranteeing the States Protection Against Invasion
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation suspends entry into the United States of all aliens "engaged in the invasion across the southern border." Such aliens are also restricting from invoking provisions of the INA that would permit their continued presence in the United States, including claims of asylum. The proclamation also suspends entry of any alien that fails to provide Federal officials with sufficient medical information and reliable criminal history and background information.

summaries.title: Holding Former Government Officials Accountable for Election Interference and Improper Disclosure of Sensitive Governmental Information
summaries.aiSummary: The EO orders the investigation of individuals and revocation of security clearances for individuals involved in the Hunter Biden laptop coverup.

summaries.title: Establishing and Implementing the President's "Department of Government Efficiency"
summaries.aiSummary: Renames the US Digital Service the United States DOGE Service (USDS) and established USDS in the Executive Office of the President. Will be led by the USDS Administrator. Establishes the US DOGE Temporary Organization dedicated to advancing the President's 18-month DOGE agenda and will terminate on July 4, 2026. Agency heads required to establish a DOGE Team of at least 4 individuals, which is tasked with advancing the DOGE Agenda. Charges the USDS Administrator with commencing a software modernization initiative.

summaries.title: America First Policy Directive to the Secretary of State
summaries.aiSummary: Requires the Secretary of State to issue guidance regarding changes to policies, programs, personnel, and operations that will focus on putting American interests first in foreign policy.

summaries.title: Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programs and Preferencing
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Director of OMB, assisted by the Attorney General and Director of OPM, to terminate all DEI and DEIA policies in the federal government. Within 60 days, all DEI, DEIA, and environmental justice offices and positions shall be terminated.

summaries.title: Realigning the United States Refugee Admissions Program
summaries.aiSummary: This EO suspends entry into the United States of refugees under the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP) until a finding is made by DHS and Sec. of State regarding whether resumption of entry of refugees under USRAP is in the interests of the United States.

summaries.title: Securing Our Borders
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes policies and procedures for DoD and DHS to secure the borders of the United States through physical barriers and increased personnel presence, apprehend and detain illegal aliens until they can be removed from the United States, and terminate parole programs and are inconsistent with the policies of the EO. The EO also requires the Secretary of State to facilitate international agreements whereby asylum seekers would remain in Mexico while their case is pending. The EO also seeks to fulfill the requirements of the DNA Fingerprint Act for all aliens detained, and to use technology to determine the validity of claimed familial relationships. The Attorney General is to prioritize the prosecution of offenses that relate to the border.

summaries.title: Unleashing American Energy
summaries.aiSummary: The EO establishes policy of fossil fuel exploration on federal lands and continental shelf, non-fuel minerals, eliminates "EV mandate", and general deregulation of energy and consumer appliances. It promotes energy exploration on federal lands, strengthens the U.S. position in mineral production, and encourages regulatory reforms to eliminate burdensome mandates and support consumer choice. The order revokes several prior climate-related EOs (13990, 13992, 14008, 14007, 14013, 14027, 14030, 14037, 14057, 14072, 14082, and 14096) and streamlines the permitting process to expedite energy project approvals. Additionally, it focuses on ensuring accurate environmental analyses and addressing national security implications related to mineral reliance.

summaries.title: Application of Protecting Americans From Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act to TikTok
summaries.aiSummary: This EO instructs the Attorney General not to enforce "The Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act" for 75 days to allow the administration to (1) consult with advisors and federal agencies or departments regarding national security concerns and (2) negotiate an appropriate resolution regarding TikTok (and any other foreign adversary controlled applications).

summaries.title: Granting Pardons And Commutation Of Sentences For Certain Offenses Relating To The Events At Or Near The United States Capitol On January 6, 2021
summaries.aiSummary: This EO instructs the Attorney General to (1) commute the sentences for 14 named individuals and (2) issue pardons to all individuals convicted of offenses at or near the US Capitol on January 6, 2021. Further, the Bureau of Prisons shall release individuals convicted of offenses at or near the US Capitol on January 6, 2021 that are currently incarcerated. Lastly, the Attorney General is directed to seek dismissals with prejudice for all pending indictments against individuals for conduct at or near the US Capitol on January 6, 2021.

summaries.title: Ending the Weaponization of the Federal Government
summaries.aiSummary: Directs the DOJ, SEC, and FTC to review all investigations during the last 4 years to determine if any investigations unfairly targeted political opponents of the Biden Administration. Also directs the DNI to determine whether the Intelligence Community has done the same. Requires these agencies to submit a report to the President identifying these matters and recommendations for appropriate remedial actions.

summaries.title: Delivering Emergency Price Relief for American Families and Defeating the Cost-of-Living Crisis
summaries.aiSummary: Deliver emergency price relief consistent with applicable law, including lowering the cost of housing, healthcare costs, costs of home appliances, and costs of food and fuel. Also requires the creation of employment opportunities for American workers.

summaries.title: Restoring the Death Penalty and Protecting Public Safety
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the US to ensure laws authorizing capital punishment are respected and implemented. The Attorney General shall pursue the death penalty "for all crimes of a severity demanding its use" including every federal capital crime involving (1) the murder of a law-enforcement officer or (2) a capital crime committed by an alien illegally present in this country. The Attorney General shall also encourage the same for state capital charges, including ensuring that states have sufficient supplies of lethal injection drugs. The EO also directs various other actions to encourage capital punishment, including: modifying the Justice Manual; evaluating the cases of the 37 individuals who received federal death sentence commutations from President Biden, including encouraging evaluation of state charges; seeking overruling of Supreme Court precedents that hinder capital punishment; and prioritizing public safety and prosecution of violent crime.

summaries.title: Reforming the Federal Hiring Process and Restoring Merit to Government Service
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs various officials (including the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy, Director of OMB, Director of OPM, and Administrator of DOGE) to develop and deliver to agency heads a new Federal Hiring Plan within 120 days. Also, the Director of OPM shall establish clear performance metrics to evaluate the success of the reforms in the new Federal Hiring Plan and request agency analysis on a regular basis.

summaries.title: Restoring Accountability for Career Senior Executives
summaries.aiSummary: Within 30 days, the Director of OPM, in coordination with the Director of OMB, shall issue SES Performance Plans that agencies must adopt. All agency heads shall reinvigorate the SES System, to include terminating and replacing the current Executive Resources Board and Performance Review Boards.

summaries.title:
Hiring Freeze 

(extended by Presidential Memo on 4/17/25, through July 15, 2025)
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs a hiring freeze for all Federal civilian employees, to be applied through the executive branch. No vacancies may be further filled or new positions created until the freeze is lifted. This freeze DOES NOT apply to military personnel of the armed forces; positions related to immigrant enforcement, national security, or public safety; anything that may adversely impact the provision of Social Security, Medicare, or Veteran's benefits; nomination and appointment of officials; or any exceptions deemed necessary by the Director of OPM. Within 90 days, the Director of OMB, in consultation with the director of OPM and Administrator of USDS, shall submit a plan to reduce the federal workforce, at which time the freeze will be lifted for all federal agencies and departments EXCEPT for the IRS. Contracting outside the federal government to circumvent this memorandum is prohibited.

summaries.title: Designating Cartels and Other Organizations as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists
summaries.aiSummary: This EO creates a process by which cartels and other organizations will be designated as Foreign Terrorist Organizations or Specially Designated Global Terrorists.

summaries.title: Return to In-Person Work
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the heads of all departments and agencies in the executive branch to take steps to terminate remote work arrangements and require employees to work in-person full time, provided that necessary exceptions are made.

summaries.title: Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce
summaries.aiSummary: This EO restores a category of federal workers known as "Schedule F" that existed in the prior Trump administration under EO 13957. Schedule F employees lack the same job protections typically enjoyed by career civil servants, including procedures and appeals rights for termination. The Director of OPM is directed to amend applicable regulations to enact the above change and issue guidance, within 30 days, about additional categories of positions for this determination.

summaries.title: Promoting Beautiful Federal Civic Architecture
summaries.aiSummary: Directs GSA to submit recommendations to the President on how to ensure Federal buildings are "visually identifiable as civic buildings and respect regional, traditional, and classical architectural heritage in order to uplift and beautify public spaces."

summaries.title: Clarifying the Military's Role in Protecting the Territorial Integrity of the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Defense to deliver a revision to the Unified Command Plan that assigns the United States Northern Command the mission to seal the borders and maintain sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security of the United States.

summaries.title: Restoring Freedom of Speech and Ending Federal Censorship
summaries.aiSummary: Prohibits federal government officers, employees, or agents from engaging in or facilitating any conduct that would restrict free speech. Prohibits use of federal resources on activities that restrict free speech. Attorney general charged with investigating activities of the Federal Government over the last 4 years that are inconsistent with policies and purposes of this EO and take remedial measures.

summaries.title: The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Global Tax Deal (Global Tax Deal)
summaries.aiSummary: Requires notice to the OECD that the Global Tax Deal has no force in the US. Rescinds any actions or commitments made by the prior administration on behalf of the United States with respect to the Global Tax Deal. Directs the Secretary of the Treasury and US Trade Representative to investigate whether any foreign countries are not in compliance with tax treaties with the US or have any tax rules in place that disproportionately affect American companies.

summaries.title: America First Trade Policy
summaries.aiSummary: Requires investigations to be conducted by Treasury, Commerce, and the Trade Representative relating to trade deficits in goods, the establishment of a External Revenue Service to collect tariffs and other foreign trade-related revenues, and the impact related to participation in US-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Also requires review of trade agreements and potential changes to these agreements, including potential new agreements on a bilateral or sector-specific basis to obtain export market access for Americans and a review of the agreements between the US and China. Commerce and DoD are tasked with conducting an economic and security review related to imports and exports.

summaries.title: Organization of the National Security Council and Subcommittees
summaries.aiSummary: Memorandum structuring the National Security Committee (NSC). It establishes the NSC as the President's principal means for coordinating national and homeland security policies across departments and agencies. The Principals Committee (PC) and Deputies Committee (DC) serve as senior interagency forums for policy development and decision-making, while Policy Coordination Committees (PCCs) manage policy implementation and integration.

summaries.title: Putting America First in International Environmental Agreements
summaries.aiSummary: The EO orders the withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, and any other agreement under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. The UN Ambassador must also immediately cease any related financial commitments.

summaries.title: Putting People over Fish: Stopping Radical Environmentalism to Provide Water to Southern California
summaries.aiSummary: The EO routes water from the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta to other parts of California.

summaries.title: Declaring a National Energy Emergency
summaries.aiSummary: The EO declares a national energy emergency due to the United States' inadequate energy supply and infrastructure. The EO directs federal agencies to utilize emergency authorities, expedite energy infrastructure projects, and leverage resources under laws like the Defense Production Act. It also calls for consultations under the Endangered Species Act to facilitate energy supply and outlines coordinated efforts to enhance the nation's energy security.

summaries.title: Unleashing Alaska's Extraordinary Resource Potential
summaries.aiSummary: The EO establishes a policy to harvest Alaska's natural resources. The EO reverses previous restrictions on resource development, particularly on state and federal lands. It mandates federal agencies to expedite permitting, leasing, and development of Alaskan resources, with a strong focus on liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects. Additionally, it requires the revision or rescission of regulations that hinder these objectives, requiring collaboration among various governmental departments to facilitate infrastructure and resource projects in Alaska.

summaries.title: Temporary Withdrawal of All Areas on the Outer Continental Shelf from Offshore Wind Leasing and Review of the Federal Government’s Leasing and Permitting Practices for Wind Projects
summaries.aiSummary: The EO "temporarily" withdraws all areas on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) from wind energy leasing to assess and review federal leasing and permitting practices for wind projects. Existing leases remain unaffected, but the EO requires a comprehensive review to be conducted to evaluate their necessity. Additionally, a temporary cessation of federal wind leasing and permitting is ordered until a thorough review is completed, with a focus on the environmental impact, legal deficiencies, and economic costs associated with wind projects.

summaries.title: Withdrawing the United States From the World Health Organization
summaries.aiSummary: Announces the intent to withdraw from the WHO. Revokes Executive Order 13987 (Organizing and Mobilizing the United States Government to Provide a Unified and Effective Response to Combat COVID–19 and to Provide United States Leadership on Global Health and Security). Pauses transfer of any government funds to the WHO and recalls/reassigns government personnel and contractors working in any capacity with the WHO. Requires review and replacement of the 2024 US Global Health Security Strategy as soon as practicable.

summaries.title: Regulatory Freeze Pending Review
summaries.aiSummary: Halts any new rules from being published in the Federal Register until a Trump appointee can review and approve. Also, directs agencies to consider postponing the effective date of any new rule published in the Federal Register for 60-days to provide additional public comment period and review by Trump appointees.

summaries.title: Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity
summaries.aiSummary: Requires all departments and agencies to terminate all discriminatory and illegal preferences, mandates, policies, programs, activities, guidance, regulations, enforcement actions, consent orders, and requirements. Rescinds executive orders and Presidential memoranda related to federal actions and initiatives to promote diversity and inclusion, including Executive Order 11246 (Equal Employment Opportunity). Directs the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to immediately cease promoting diversity and holding federal contractors and subcontractors responsible for taking affirmative action. Does not apply to employment and contracting preferences for veterans. Requires each agency head to include in every contract or grant award a term/provision that makes compliance with all applicable Federal anti-discrimination laws material to the government's payment decisions, which includes a certification that the contractor/recipient does not operate any DEI programs that violate any applicable Federal anti-discrimination laws. Directs federal agencies to encourage private sector to advance the policy of individual initiative, excellence, and hard work.

summaries.title: Revocation of Certain Executive Orders
summaries.aiSummary: This EO revokes: (a) Executive Order 14042 of September 9, 2021 (Ensuring Adequate COVID Safety Protocols for Federal Contractors); and (b) Executive Order 14043 of September 9, 2021 (Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees).

summaries.title: Keeping Americans Safe in Aviation
summaries.aiSummary: Directs DoT and FAA to "return to non-discriminatory, merit-based hiring, as required by law" and rescinds all DEI initiatives at these agencies.

summaries.title: Designation of Ansar Allah as a Foreign Terrorist Organization
summaries.aiSummary: This EO initiates the process of designating the Ansar Allah, also known as the Houthis, as a Foreign Terrorist Organization.

summaries.title: Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology
summaries.aiSummary: This EO rescinds EO 14067 and directs the Secretary of Treasury to take appropriate actions consistent with this new EO regarding the digital sector. Further, the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets is established, to be chaired by the Special Advisor for AI and Crypto. The Working Group is responsible for analyzing the digital sector and making recommendations.

summaries.title: President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) which shall advise the President on matters involving science, technology, education, and innovation policy and provide the President with scientific and technical information that is needed to inform public policy relating to the American economy, the American worker, national and homeland security, and other topics.

summaries.title: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence
summaries.aiSummary: This EO instructs APST, APNSA, Special Advisor for AI and Crypto, in coordination with the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy, the OMB Director, and any heads of relevant agencies to develop an AI Action Plan. The AI Action Plan should be free of "social agendas."  The EO further orders a review of actions taken pursuant to EO 14110 (rescinded) and a correction of any agency actions that are not consistent with this EO.

summaries.title: Declassification of Records Concerning the Assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Senator Robert F. Kennedy, and the Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Director of National Intelligence and AG to present a plan to the President for the full and complete release of records relating to the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. Further, the Director of National Intelligence and the AG shall review records related to the assassinations of Senator Robert F. Kennedy and the Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., and present a plan to the President for the full and complete release of these records.

summaries.title: Memorandum for the Secretary of State the Secretary of Defense the Secretary of Health and Human Services the Administrator of the United States for International Development – The White House
summaries.aiSummary: This memo revokes the 1/28/21 PM and reinstates the 1/23/17 PM, also called The Mexico Policy. Further, the Secretary of State is directed to implement a plan to extend the requirements for the reinstated PM to global health assistance furnished by all departments or agencies. The Secretary of State shall also take actions to ensure that US taxpayer dollars do not fund organizations or programs that participate in coercive abortion or involuntary sterilization.

summaries.title: Council To Assess the Federal Emergency Management Agency
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes a FEMA Review Council to assess and improve FEMA's effectiveness and impartiality in disaster response. The Council, led by the Secretaries of DHS and DoD, will include government and external experts. It will advise the President and produce a report with assessments and reform recommendations. The Council will terminate after one year unless extended.

summaries.title: Enforcing the Hyde Amendment
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of this administration, consistent with the Hyde Amendment, to end Federal taxpayer funds for elective abortion. Further, it revokes EO 14076 (Protecting Access to Reproductive Healthcare Services) and EO 14079 (Securing Access to Reproductive and Other Healthcare Services). The Director of OMB shall promulgate guidance to the heads of executive departments and agencies related to implementation.

summaries.title: Emergency Measures To Provide Water Resources in California and Improve Disaster Response in Certain Areas
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs various Secretaries (Defense, Homeland Security, Interior, Commerce, Agriculture) to ensure water resources in Southern California, including: override activities impeding water delivery, maximize water delivery through the Central Valley Project (CVP), expedite exemptions under the Endangered Species Act for water projects, and identify and address regulatory hurdles for water-supply projects. Further, OMB shall review Federal programs affecting land and water management, with recommendations to ensure compliance and disaster prevention.

summaries.title: The Iron Dome for America
summaries.aiSummary: This EO prioritizes missile defense for the homeland. Under this EO, the Secretary of Defense shall present an architecture and implementation plan for a next-generation missile defense shield for the US. Further, the US shall continue to cooperate with allies and partners on missile defense to protect allies and US troops abroad.

summaries.title: National Day of Remembrance of the 80th Anniversary of the Liberation of Auschwitz, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This memo proclaims 1/27/25 as National Day of Remembrance of the 80th Anniversary of the Liberation of Auschwitz.

summaries.title: Restoring America's Fighting Force
summaries.aiSummary: This EO orders the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Homeland security, as it relates to the Coast Guard, shall abolish every DEI office. Secretary of Defense shall conduct an internal review of any actions taking in pursuit of DEI initiatives. DoD and Armed Forces, including any educational institution under its control, is prohibited from promoting DEI or any listed gender ideology theories.

summaries.title: Reinstating Service Members Discharged Under the Military's COVID-19 Vaccination Mandate
summaries.aiSummary: This EO creates avenues for reinstatement of military members to be reinstated if they were previously discharged for refusing to comply with Covid-19 vaccination requirements.

summaries.title: Protecting Children From Chemical and Surgical Mutilation
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that "it is the policy of the United States that it will not fund, sponsor, promote, assist, or support the so-called “transition” of a child from one sex to another, and it will rigorously enforce all laws that prohibit or limit these destructive and life-altering procedures." The EO directs specific actions at HHS, DoD, and DOJ to enforce this, including stopping insurance support, reviewing policies, and requiring this policy for all federally funded organizations.

summaries.title: Celebrating America's 250th Birthday
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the "White House Task Force on Celebrating America's 250th Birthday" to coordinate the celebration of the 250th anniversary of American independence. Further, EO 13934 (Building and Rebuilding Monuments to American Heroes), 13978 (Building the National Garden of American Heroes), and 13922 (Protecting American Monuments, Memorials, and Statues and Combatting Recent Criminal Violence) are reinstated.

summaries.title: Expanding Educational Freedom and Opportunity for Families
summaries.aiSummary: This EO supports school of choice. Specifically, this EO directs the Secretary of Education to include education freedom as a priority in discretionary grant programs and issue guidance regarding how states can use federal formula funds to support K-12 education choice initiatives. The EO further directs the Secretaries of Labor, HHS, DoD, and Interior to review available mechanisms to further this policy

summaries.title: Ending Radical Indoctrination in K-12 Schooling
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to prohibit recipients of federal funds providing K-12 education from using "discriminatory" ideologies, primarily based on race, color, sex, or national origin. Various heads of agencies are directed to draft policy recommendations to enforce this EO. Further, the "1776 Commission" is reestablished with the goal of promoting patriotic education. All relevant agencies are directed to monitor compliance with the requirement that all educational institutions with federal funds hold a yearly constitution education program.

summaries.title: Expanding Migrant Operations Center at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay to Full Capacity
summaries.aiSummary: This Memo directs the Secretaries of Defense and Homeland Security to take appropriate actions to expand the Migrant Operations Center at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay to full capacity to provide additional detention space for high-priority criminal aliens unlawfully present in the US and to address immigration enforcement needs.

summaries.title: Additional Measures To Combat Anti-Semitism
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the heads of each agency or executive department to submit a report to the President identifying authorities that might be used to curb or combat anti-Semitism and listing an inventory and analysis of pending complaints of civil-rights violations with anti-semitism against or involving higher education institutions. The Attorney General is also directed to submit a report and analysis of all cases involving higher education institutions and post-October 7, 2023 antisemitism. The Secretaries of State, Education, and Homeland Security must also report recommendations for familiarizing higher education institutions with grounds of inadmissibility under 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(3) for "aliens."

summaries.title: Limiting Lame-Duck Collective Bargaining Agreements That Improperly Attempt to Constrain the New President
summaries.aiSummary: This memo was sent to the heads of all executive departments and agencies and states that the policy of the executive branch is that Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs) executed in the 30 days prior to the inauguration of a new president that purport to remain effective under the new administration shall not be approved. The memo bars CBAs executed in the 30 days prior to the inauguration with new contractual obligations, substantive changes to the existing agreements, or extending the duration of the existing agreement. This does not apply to CBAs covering law enforcement officers.

summaries.title: Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that whenever an agency publicly proposes for notice and comment or otherwise promulgates a new regulation, it shall identify at least 10 existing regulations to be repealed. For FY 2025, the heads of all agencies are directed to ensure that the total incremental cost of all new regulations being finalized this year shall be significantly less than zero. Any new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least 10 prior regulations. Further, for each agency's Regulatory Plan, the agency head must identify the increased costs and the offsetting regulations with total costs or savings associated with each of these. No regulation shall be issued by an agency if it was not included in the most recent update of the Unified Regulatory Agenda. The Director of OMB is charged with implementing this order, including providing additional guidance to the agencies.

summaries.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Situation at Our Southern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO expands the scope of the national emergency declared under Proclamation 10886 to include the failure of Mexico to arrest, seize, detain, or otherwise intercept drug trafficking organizations (DTOs), other drug and human traffickers, criminals, and illicit drugs. Further, a 25% ad valorem rate of duty  is imposed on all products of Mexico, beginning 2/4/25, except for goods entered for consumption. The Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to modify the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the US (HTSUS) to effect this order. The tariff does not apply to products eligible for admission under "domestic status" as defined in 19 CFR 146.43. Further, the Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to consult regularly with Secretary of State, AG, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security regarding the situation on the southern border. Secretary of Homeland Security must consult with Secretaries of Treasury and Commerce and AG to adopt rules and regulations to enforce this EO.  All agencies shall take appropriate action to enforce this EO.

summaries.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This EO expands the scope of the national emergency declared under Proclamation 10886 to include the failure of the PRC to arrest, seize, detain, or otherwise intercept chemical precursor suppliers, money launderers, other transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), criminals, and drugs. Further, a 10% ad valorem rate of duty is imposed on all products of PRC, beginning 2/4/25, except for goods entered for consumption. The Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to modify the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the US (HTSUS) to effect this order. The tariff does not apply to products eligible for admission under "domestic status" as defined in 19 CFR 146.43. Further, the Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to consult regularly with Secretary of State, AG, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security regarding the PRC. Secretary of Homeland Security must consult with Secretaries of Treasury and Commerce and AG to adopt rules and regulations to enforce this EO. All agencies shall take appropriate action to enforce this EO.

summaries.title: Imposing Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO expands the scope of the national emergency declared under Proclamation 10886 to include the failure of Canada to arrest, seize, detain, or otherwise intercept drug trafficking organizations (DTOs), other drug and human traffickers, criminals, and drugs. Further, a 25% ad valorem rate of duty is imposed on all products of Canada, beginning 2/4/25, except for goods entered for consumption. There is also an exception for energy resources, which are subject to a 10% ad valorem  rate of duty (not 25%). The Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to modify the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the US (HTSUS) to effect this order. The tariff does not apply to products eligible for admission under "domestic status" as defined in 19 CFR 146.43. Further, the Secretary of Homeland Security is directed to consult regularly with Secretary of State, AG, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security regarding the situation on the northern border. Secretary of Homeland Security must consult with Secretaries of Treasury and Commerce and AG to adopt rules and regulations to enforce this EO.  All agencies shall take appropriate action to enforce this EO.

summaries.title: Progress on the Situation at Our Northern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO pauses the EO issued on 2/1/25, Imposing Duties to Address the Situation at Our Northern Border, until 3/4/25. The Secretary of Homeland Security shall consult with the Secretary of State, AG, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and Assistant to the President for Homeland Security and continue to assess the situation.

summaries.title: Progress on the Situation at Our Southern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO pauses the EO issued on 2/1/25, Imposing Duties to Address the Situation at Our Southern Border, until 3/4/25. The Secretary of Homeland Security shall consult with the Secretary of State, AG, Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and Assistant to the President for Homeland Security and continue to assess the situation.

summaries.title: A Plan for Establishing a United States Sovereign Wealth Fund
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretaries of the Treasury and Commerce, in coordination with the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, to develop a plan for the establishment of a sovereign wealth fund and submit it to the President within 90 days.

summaries.title: National Security Presidential Memorandum/NSPM-2
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to impose "maximum pressure" on the Iranian regime to end its nuclear threat. This includes directing the Secretary of Treasury to impose sanctions and update its policies for Iranian terror proxies; the Secretary of State to impose sanctions and lead campaigns to drive Iran's export of oil to zero and isolate Iran from the rest of the world; US Permanent Representative to the UN to work with allies to further this goal; Secretary of Commerce to conduct export control enforcement of military items; and AG to pursue legal steps to disrupt Iran and its terror proxy.

summaries.title: Withdrawing the United States From and Ending Funding to Certain United Nations Organizations and Reviewing United States Support to All International Organizations
summaries.aiSummary: This EO terminates US participation with UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC) and directs a review of US participation with the UN Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Further, US agencies shall not contribute any funds to UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). The Secretary of State and UN Ambassador shall conduct a review of all international intergovernmental organizations that the US is a member of and provides funding to. Lastly, the Secretary of State shall inform the UN that the US will not satisfy any claims to 2025 payments to these organizations.

summaries.title: Amendment to Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This EO amends the previous EO on duties to PRC to allow duty-free de minimis treatment for some specific eligible articles.

summaries.title: Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to rescind all federal funds to educational programs that allow male competitive participation in women's sports. The Secretary of Education is directed to affirmatively protect all-female athletic opportunities and locker rooms under Title IX. Further, the Secretary of Education and AG will prioritize Title IX enforcement in this manner. All agencies will review grants to educational programs and rescind funding for failure to comply with this order. Various agencies will also do affirmative outreach to state and other organizations to promote this policy, including athletic organizations and governing bodies.

summaries.title: Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court
summaries.aiSummary: This EO prevents any payment to specific persons who had directly engaged in an effort by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute a protected person without the consent of that person's country or materially support a barred activity. Further, certain immigrant entry into the US is suspended. Other various fiscal sanctions are imposed.

summaries.title: Eradicating Anti-Christian Bias
summaries.aiSummary: This EO creates a Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias, which must review the activities of all executive agencies and determine any anti-Christian policies or practices and make corrective recommendations.

summaries.title: Memorandum for the Heads of Executive Departments and Agencies
summaries.aiSummary: This memo directs the heads of all agencies to review all funding provided to NGOs and align future funding with the goals and interests of the US and this administration.

summaries.title: Establishment of the White House Faith Office
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the White House Faith Office which will advise the President on policy that may impact the ability for faith-based organizations to serve their communities.

summaries.title: Addressing Egregious Actions of the Republic of South Africa
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that the US (including all US agencies) will not provide aid or assistance to South Africa, and halt any current aid. Further, the US will promote the resettlement of Afrikaner refugees escaping government-sponsored race-based discrimination. The heads of any agencies may permit foreign aid or assistance deems necessary. DHS and Secretary of State shall prioritize relief to assist the Afrikaners group.

summaries.title: Protecting Second Amendment Rights
summaries.aiSummary: AG will examine all policies and plans to assess any ongoing infringements on the Second Amendment.

summaries.title: Adjusting Imports of Steel into the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation suspends previous proclamations regarding steel imports from various countries as of 3/12/2025. Further, a 25% ad valorem rate of duty is implemented for all imports of steels and aluminum into the US beginning 3/12/25 with no exceptions. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for additional steel ad valorem duties within 90 days.

summaries.title: Pausing Foreign Corrupt Practices Act Enforcement To Further American Economic and National Security
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the AG to review policies governing the investigations and enforcement actions under the FCPA for a period of 180 days. This review shall include a pause of any new investigations. The AG may extend this for an additional 180 days if deemed appropriate.

summaries.title: Ending Procurement and Forced Use of Paper Straws
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the heads of each agency or department to take appropriate action to eliminate the procurement of paper straws within agency buildings and eliminate policies designed to disfavor plastic straws.

summaries.title: Eliminating the Federal Executive Institute
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs OMB to take all necessary steps to eliminate the Federal Executive Institute.

summaries.title: Adjusting Imports of Aluminum into the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation suspends previous proclamations regarding aluminum imports from various countries as of 3/12/2025. Further, a 25% ad valorem rate of duty is implemented for all imports of aluminum into the US beginning 3/12/25 with no exceptions. All aluminum and aluminum derivative articles from Russia or containing Russian aluminum will be subject to a 200% ad valorem rate. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to establish a process for additional steel ad valorem duties within 90 days.

summaries.title: Implementing the President's "Department of Government Efficiency" Workforce Optimization Initiative
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs Director of OMB to submit a plan to reduce the size of the federal government's workforce through efficiency improvements and attrition. This plan must require each agency to hire no more than one employee for every four that depart. This EO does not apply to functions related to public safety, immigration enforcement, or law enforcement. Each agency must develop a hiring plan in compliance with this EO and cannot fill any vacancies that the DOGE team determines should not be filled, unless the agency head determines otherwise. Agency heads shall promptly undertake preparations to initiate large-scale reductions in force. OPM shall initiate a rulemaking process to revise 5 CFR 731.202(b) to include additional suitability criteria. This EO does not apply to military personnel, any positions deemed by agency heads to be necessary for national security, homeland security, or public safety, and any exemptions granted by Director of OPM.

summaries.title: One Voice for America's Foreign Relations
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that all officers or employees charged with implementing the foreign policy of the US must do so under the direction of the President and failure to implement the President's policy is grounds for professional discipline, including separation. When the Secretary of State concludes that an employee warrants personnel action, the Secretary may, at his or her discretion, refer the matter to the President. The Secretary shall reform the Foreign Service to ensure faithful implementation of the President's agenda, including recruiting, evaluation, retention standards, and update the manual and any other policies as needed.

summaries.title: Establishing the President's Make America Healthy Again Commission
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs all executive departments and agencies that address health or healthcare to focus on reversing chronic disease, including the following actions: all federally funded health research should use transparency and open-source data and eliminate conflicts of interest; NIH and other federal health research initiatives should prioritize research on chronic illness; agencies should work with farmers to ensure US food is healthy, abundant, and affordable; and agencies should ensure availability of expanded treatment options and flexible insurance coverage for lifestyle changes/disease prevention. Further, the Make America Healthy Again Commission is established with the initial mission to advise the President how to address childhood chronic disease (reports due in 100 days and 180 days).

summaries.title: Establishing the National Energy Dominance Council
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the National Energy Dominance Council, with the Secretary of the Interior as Chair and Secretary of Energy as Vice Chair. This Council shall advise the President on how to best exercise authority to produce more energy in America, advise the President on how to improve the processes for permitting, production, generation, distribution, regulation, transportation, and export of American energy, provide a recommended National Energy Dominance Strategy to produce more energy, and advise the President on facilitating public-private energy partnerships.

summaries.title: Keeping Education Accessible and Ending COVID-19 Vaccine Mandates in Schools
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Education to issue guidelines to schools (including elementary schools, local educational agencies, State educational agencies, secondary schools, and institutions of higher education) regarding the legal obligations for Covid-19 school mandates. Further, the Secretary of HHS and Education shall create a plan to implement these guidelines, including a list of non-compliant schools and suggested corrective agency action.

summaries.title: Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the executive branch to "ensure Presidential supervision and control of the entire executive branch" and all executive agencies (including independent agencies) shall "submit for review all proposed and final significant regulatory actions to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) within the Executive Office of the President before publication in the Federal Register." This does not apply to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System or to the Federal Open Market Committee. Definitions for various independent agencies and employees subject to this EO are provided. Director of OMB shall establish performance standards and management objectives for independent agency heads and report their performance and efficiency to the President periodically. Director of OMB shall also review independent regulatory agencies' obligations for consistency with the President's policies regularly and consult with agency chairmen to adjust agency actions as necessary and appropriate to advance the President's policies, which may include prohibiting expending of appropriations on particular activities. Further, the heads of independent regulatory agencies shall each establish a White House Liaison, regularly consult with directors of OMB, White House Domestic Policy, and White House National Economic Council, and submit strategic plans to the Director of OMB for clearance prior to finalization. Lastly, the President and the AG (subject to President's supervision and control) shall provide the authoritative interpretations of law for the executive branch, which is controlling on all executive employees in their official duties.

summaries.title: Expanding Access to In Vitro Fertilization
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy to submit a list of policy recommendations on protecting IVF access and reducing out-of-pocket and health plan costs for IVF treatment to the President within 90 days.

summaries.title: Radical Transparency About Wasteful Spending
summaries.aiSummary: This Memo directs the heads of agencies to take appropriate actions to make public (as legal and appropriate) the complete details of every terminated program, cancelled contract, terminated grant, or any other discontinued obligation of federal funds.

summaries.title: 80th Anniversary of the Battle of Iwo Jima
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims February 19, 2025, as the 80th Anniversary of the Battle of Iwo Jima.

summaries.title: Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Open Borders
summaries.aiSummary: Thie EO directs the head of each agency to (1) identify all federally funded programs administered by the agency that currently permits illegal aliens to obtain any cash or non-cash public benefit and take appropriate actions to align such programs with this order and federal law; (2) ensure federal payments to states and localities do not facilitate the subsidization or promotion of illegal immigration (i.e. "sanctuary policies"); (3) enhance eligibility verification systems to ensure benefits exclude any ineligible alien. Director of OMB and DOGE Administrator shall further identify sources of federal funding for illegal aliens and recommend agency actions. Agencies are directed to refer any improper receipt of funds to DOJ and DHS for appropriate action.

summaries.title: Commencing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the elimination of non-statutory components and functions of the following agencies:  the Presidio Trust; the Inter-American Foundation; the United States African Development Foundation; and the United States Institute of Peace. Within 14 days, the head of each of the above agencies shall submit a report to OMB Director confirming compliance with this EO and stating what components are statutorily required and to what extent. Funding to these agencies should be rejected unless compliant with this EO. The Presidential Memorandum of November 13, 1961 (Need for Greater Coordination of Regional and Field Activities of the Government), is revoked. OPM Director shall initiate the process to withdraw regulations 5 CFR 960 (Federal Executive Boards) and 5 CFR 362 (Presidential Management Fellows program). Within 14 days, the applicable heads shall terminate the following agencies:  Advisory Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid, Academic Research Council and the Credit Union Advisory Council, Community Bank Advisory Council, Secretary’s Advisory Committee on Long COVID, and Health Equity Advisory Committee. Within 30 days, assistants to the President shall submit a list of other government entities that should be terminated as unnecessary.

summaries.title: Ensuring Lawful Governance and Implementing the President's "Department of Government Efficiency" Deregulatory Initiative
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs agency heads, in coordination with their DOGE Team Leads and the Director of OMB, to initiate a process to review all regulations subject to their sole or joint jurisdiction for consistency with law and Administration policy. Within 60 days, the agency heads shall submit a list of various classes of identified regulations. The Administrator of OIRA shall consult with the agency heads to develop a Unified Regulatory Agenda that seeks to rescind or modify these regulations as appropriate. Further, agencies shall seek to preserve their enforcement resources by de-prioritizing actions to enforce regulations that are based on anything other than the best reading of the statute or goes beyond constitutional power. Agency heads shall consult with their DOGE Team Leads and Administrator of OIRA on potential new regulations as soon as practicable. This does NOT apply to: military, national security, homeland security, foreign affairs, immigration, executive branch management of its employees, and anything else exempted by Director of OMB.

summaries.title: Defending American Companies and Innovators from Overseas Extortion and Unfair Fines and Penalties
summaries.aiSummary: This memo states that it is the policy of this administration that when a foreign government imposes a fine, penalty, tax, or other burden that is discriminatory, disproportionate, or designed to transfer significant funds or intellectual property from American companies to the foreign government, this Administration will act, imposing tariffs and taking such other responsive actions necessary to mitigate the harm to the United States. This memo directs the US Trade Representative to determine whether to renew various investigations of DSTs in specific countries. The Secretary of Treasury, Secretary of Commerce, and US Trade Representative shall identify trade and other regulatory practices by other countries that discriminate against or disproportionately affect US global competitiveness in the digital economy OR limit free speech and recommend appropriate actions to counter this.

summaries.title: America First Investment Policy: U.S. Foreign Investment Policy Evolves under Trump 2.0
summaries.aiSummary: This memo outlines a variety of policies that will further American investment particularly in emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, while safeguarding national security, including the following: The U.S. aims to be a top destination for investment, benefiting from allied and partner contributions; Limitations will be placed on foreign investments in critical sectors unless investors are verifiably independent from adversaries like the PRC; A streamlined process will be created to encourage investments from allies in U.S. advanced technology; Expedited environmental reviews for investments over $1 billion; New rules will prevent PRC-affiliated entities from acquiring critical American businesses and assets; Strengthening CFIUS to restrict adversary investments in strategic sectors and technologies; Encouraging non-controlling foreign investments that do not affect national security; Using legal tools to prevent U.S. investments in the PRC's military-industrial sector; Considering restrictions on U.S. investments in strategic sectors in the PRC; Evaluating the suspension of the 1984 U.S.-PRC Income Tax Convention to encourage domestic investment; Ensuring foreign companies meet auditing standards, reviewing structures limiting investor rights, and upholding fiduciary standards. The agencies are directed to implement the above policy as appropriate.

summaries.title: Suspension of Security Clearances and Evaluation of Government Contracts
summaries.aiSummary: This memo directs the AG and all other relevant heads of agencies to take steps to suspend any active security clearances held by Peter Koski and all members, partners, and employees of Covington & Burling LLP who assisted former Special Counsel Jack Smith during his time as Special Counsel, pending a review and determination of their roles and responsibilities, if any, in the weaponization of the judicial process. Further, the agencies shall take all necessary actions to terminate any engagement of Covington & Burling LLP and review all current government contracts with the firm.

summaries.title: Addressing the Threat to National Security From Imports of Copper
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the US to ensure a reliable, secure, and resilient domestic copper supply chain. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to initiate an investigation under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act to determine the effects on national security of imports of copper in all forms and assess it based on 19 U.S.C. 1862(d) factors, and other factors as listed by the EO. The Secretary of Commerce shall consult with Secretaries of Defense, Energy, and Interior to evaluate national security risks associated with copper import dependency.

summaries.title: Making America Healthy Again by Empowering Patients With Clear, Accurate, and Actionable Healthcare Pricing Information
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that the Federal Government will promote universal access to clear and accurate healthcare prices. The Secretaries of the Treasury, Labor, and HHS are directed to take all necessary and appropriate action to rapidly implement and enforce the healthcare price transparency regulations issued pursuant to Executive Order 13877 (June 24, 2019, Improving Price and Quality Transparency in American Healthcare to Put Patients First) to require the disclosure of the actual prices of items and services, not estimates, issue updated guidance or proposed regulatory action ensuring pricing information is standardized and easily comparable across hospitals and health plans, and issue guidance or proposed regulatory action updating enforcement policies designed to ensure compliance with the transparent reporting of complete, accurate, and meaningful data within 90 days.

summaries.title: Implementing the President's "Department of Government Efficiency" Cost Efficiency Initiative
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs each agency head to build a centralized technological system within the agency to record every payment by the agency with a brief written justification by the employee who approved it. The system shall also include a mechanism for the agency head to pause and rapidly review any payment that does not include a written justification. If possible, the written justifications should be posted publicly. Further, each agency head shall review (1) all existing contracts and grants and terminate or modify those that do not align with this administration’s policies within 30 days and (2) the agency’s contracting policies, procedures, and personnel within 30 days and shall not approve new contracting officer warrants during this time unless deemed necessary. Following this review, agency heads shall issue guidance on signing or modifying contracts and the DOGE Team Lead will write a monthly report on this. Also, a written justification will be required for non-essential travel. As possible, all agency employee credit cards shall be treated as frozen for 30 days, except for those used for disaster relief, natural disaster response, or critical services. Lastly, agencies shall (1) confirm submitted updates regarding real property (7 days), (2) identify all termination rights under current leases (30 days), and (3) submit a plan to OMB for disposition of real-property that is no longer needed (60 days). This order does not apply to the following: law enforcement officers, USCBP and ICE, Uniformed Services, any other grant, contract, component, or real property deemed exempt, and classified information/systems.

summaries.title: Addressing the Threat to National Security From Imports of Timber, Lumber, and Their Derivative Products
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is the policy of the US to ensure reliable, secure, and resilient domestic supply chains of timber, lumber, and their derivative products. Further, the US must explore whether subsidies and foreign government support for foreign timber, lumber, and their derivative products necessitates action under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act to evaluate the impact on national security. This EO directs the Secretary of Commerce to initiate an investigation under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act to determine the effects on the national security of imports of timber, lumber, and their derivative products. Further, The Secretary of Commerce shall consult with the Secretary of Defense and the heads of other relevant agencies to evaluate the national security risks associated with imports of timber, lumber, and their derivative products and submit a report to the President.

summaries.title: Designating English as the Official Language of the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This EO designates English as the official language of the US. Further, EO 13166 of August 11, 2000 (Improving Access to Services for Persons with Limited English Proficiency), is revoked. However, Agency heads are not required to amend, remove, or otherwise stop production of documents, products, or other services prepared or offered in languages other than English. The AG shall remove any policy guidance documents issued pursuant to EO 13166.

summaries.title: Immediate Expansion of American Timber Production
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to implement various policy changes and guidance to increase the production of timber, lumber, paper, bioenergy, and other wood products.

summaries.title: Amendment to Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO further amends Executive Order 14193 of February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties to Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border), as amended by Executive Order 14197 of February 3, 2025 (Progress on the Situation at Our Northern Border), to include: Duty-free de minimis treatment under 19 U.S.C. 1321 for otherwise eligible covered articles described in subsection (a) and subsection (b). Further, this duty free de minimis treatment shall not be available for such otherwise eligible covered articles upon notification by the Secretary of Commerce to the President that adequate systems are in place to fully and expeditiously process and collect tariff revenue for covered articles otherwise eligible for de minimis treatment.

summaries.title: Amendment to Duties To Address the Situation at Our Southern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO further amends Executive Order 14194 of February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties to Address the Situation at Our Southern Border), as amended by Executive Order 14198 of February 3, 2025 (Progress on the Situation at Our Southern Border), to include: Duty-free de minimis treatment under 19 U.S.C. 1321 for otherwise eligible covered articles described in subsection (a) and subsection (b). Further, this duty free de minimis treatment shall not be available for such otherwise eligible covered articles upon notification by the Secretary of Commerce to the President that adequate systems are in place to fully and expeditiously process and collect tariff revenue for covered articles otherwise eligible for de minimis treatment.

summaries.title: Further Amendment to Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that the PRC has not taken adequate steps to alleviate the illicit drug crisis. Further, it amends Executive Order 14195 to raise ad valorem tariffs on articles that are products of the PRC from 10% to 20%.

summaries.title: Honoring Jocelyn Nungaray
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of the Interior to take appropriate actions to rename the area known as the “Anahuac National Wildlife Refuge” to the “Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge.”

summaries.title: Amendment to Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Southern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO adjusts the tariffs imposed on articles of Canada in Executive Order 14194 of February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties to Address the Situation at Our Southern Border). Specifically, articles that are entered free of duty as a good of Mexico under the terms of general note 11 to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), including any treatment set forth in subchapter XXIII of chapter 98 and subchapter XXII of chapter 99 of the HTSUS, as related to the Agreement between the United States of America, United Mexican States, and Canada, shall not be subject to the additional ad valorem rate of duty described in section 2(a) of Executive Order 14194. Further, the additional rate of duty on potash that is not subject to subsection (a) of this section shall be reduced to 10 percent in lieu of 25 percent. This EO is set to go into effect on March 7, 2025.

summaries.title: Amendment to Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO adjusts the tariffs imposed on articles of Canada in Executive Order 14193 of February 1, 2025 (Imposing Duties to Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border). Specifically, articles that are entered free of duty as a good of Canada under the terms of general note 11 to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), including any treatment set forth in subchapter XXIII of chapter 98 and subchapter XXII of chapter 99 of the HTSUS, as related to the Agreement between the United States of America, United Mexican States, and Canada, shall not be subject to the additional ad valorem rate of duty described in section 2(a) or section 2(b) of Executive Order 14193. Further, the additional rate of duty on potash that is not subject to subsection (a) of this section shall be reduced to 10 percent in lieu of 25 percent. This EO is set to go into effect on March 7, 2025.

summaries.title: Establishment of the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and United States Digital Asset Stockpile
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of the Treasury shall establish an office to administer and maintain control of custodial accounts collectively known as the “Strategic Bitcoin Reserve,” capitalized with all BTC held by the Department of the Treasury that was finally forfeited as part of criminal or civil asset forfeiture proceedings or in satisfaction of any civil money penalty imposed by any executive department or agency (agency) and that is not needed to satisfy requirements under 31 U.S.C. 9705 or released pursuant to subsection (d) of this section (Government BTC) Further, the Secretary of the Treasury shall establish an office to administer and maintain control of custodial accounts collectively known as the “United States Digital Asset Stockpile,” The Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of Commerce shall develop strategies for acquiring additional Government BTC.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks From Perkins Coie LLP
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs various types of review, to include security clearances, contracting, and racial discrimination within Perkins Coie LLP. Specifically, the Director of National Intelligence is directed to take steps to suspend any active security clearances held by individuals at Perkins Coie pending review and review any sensitive government information provided to Perkins Coie and cease such provision. Further, agencies shall disclose any government contracting business done with Perkins Coie and review all current contracts or entities that disclose doing business with Perkins Coie, and take appropriate steps to terminate any contract for which Perkins Coie has been hired to perform any service. Further, the Chair of the EEOC shall review and the AG shall investigate the practices of large law firms for consistency with Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, including whether large law firms: reserve certain positions for individuals of preferred races; promote individuals on a discriminatory basis; permit client access on a discriminatory basis; or provide access to events, trainings, or travel on a discriminatory basis. Heads of agencies shall provide guidance limiting official access from Federal Government buildings to employees of Perkins Coie when such access would threaten the national security of or otherwise be inconsistent with the interests of the United States and provide guidance limiting Government employees acting in their official capacity from engaging with Perkins Coie employees to ensure consistency with the national security and other interests of the United States. Agency officials shall refrain from hiring employees of Perkins Coie, absent a waiver from the head of the agency.

summaries.title: Restoring Public Service Loan Forgiveness
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Education to propose revisions to the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program, in coordination with the Secretary of the Treasury as appropriate, that ensure the definition of “public service” excludes organizations that engage in activities that have a substantial illegal purpose, including: aiding or abetting violations of Federal immigration laws; supporting terrorism; engaging in violence for the purpose of obstructing or influencing Federal Government policy; child abuse, including “chemical and surgical castration or mutilation of children or the trafficking of children to other States. . .for purposes of emancipation from their lawful parents, in violation of applicable law[;]” aiding and abetting illegal discrimination; or violating State tort laws, including laws against trespassing, disorderly conduct, public nuisance, vandalism, and obstruction of highways.

summaries.title: Establishing the White House Task Force on the FIFA World Cup 2026
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the White House Task Force on the FIFA World Cup 2026. Agencies within the Task Force shall each provide a report to the Task Force regarding their respective planning and activities with respect to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

summaries.title: U.S. Hostage and Wrongful Detainee Day, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims March 9, 2025, as U.S. Hostage and Wrongful Detainee Day.

summaries.title: Ensuring the Enforcement of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 65(c)
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation states that it is the policy of the United States to demand that parties seeking injunctions against the Federal Government must cover the costs and damages incurred if the Government is ultimately found to have been wrongfully enjoined or restrained and that “Federal courts should hold litigants accountable for their misrepresentations and ill-granted injunctions.” The heads of agencies shall, in consultation with the Attorney General, ensure that their respective agencies properly request under Rule 65(c) that Federal district courts require plaintiffs to post security equal to the Federal Government’s potential costs and damages from a wrongly issued injunction. The scope of this directive covers all lawsuits filed against the Federal Government seeking an injunction where agencies can show expected monetary damages or costs from the requested preliminary relief, unless extraordinary circumstances justify an exception.

summaries.title: Additional Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions
summaries.aiSummary: This EO rescinds various past executive orders and presidential actions. For a complete list of rescinded actions, see the next tab.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks From Paul Weiss
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs a suspension pending review for any active security clearances held by individuals at Paul Weiss and Mark Pomerantz and a cessation of any government materials provided. Government contracting agencies shall, to the extent permissible by law, require Government contractors to disclose any business they do with Paul Weiss and whether that business is related to the subject of the Government contract. The heads of all agencies shall review all contracts with Paul Weiss or with entities that disclose doing business with Paul Weiss under subsection and take steps to terminate any contracts. The heads of all agencies shall provide guidance limiting official access from Federal Government buildings to employees of Paul Weiss when such access would threaten the national security of or otherwise be inconsistent with the interests of the United States and guidance limiting Government employees acting in their official capacity from engaging with Paul Weiss employees. Lastly, agency officials shall refrain from hiring employees of Paul Weiss, absent a waiver from the head of the agency, made in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

summaries.title: Continuing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy
summaries.aiSummary:
Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, the non-statutory components and functions of the following governmental entities shall be eliminated to the maximum extent consistent with applicable law: (i) the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service; (ii) the United States Agency for Global Media; (iii) the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars in the Smithsonian Institution; (iv)   the Institute of Museum and Library Services; (v) the United States Interagency Council on Homelessness; (vi) the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund; and (vii) the Minority Business Development Agency.
In reviewing budget requests submitted by the governmental entities listed, the Director of OMB or the head of any agency charged with reviewing grant requests by such entities shall reject funding requests for such governmental entities to the extent they are inconsistent with this order.

summaries.title: Invocation of the Alien Enemies Act Regarding the Invasion of the United States by Tren De Aragua
summaries.aiSummary: This Proclamation declares that Tren De Aragua (“TdA”) is perpetrating, attempting, and threatening an invasion or predatory incursion against the territory of the United States and that all Venezuelan citizens 14 years of age or older who are members of TdA, are within the United States, and are not actually naturalized or lawful permanent residents of the United States are liable to be apprehended, restrained, secured, and removed as Alien Enemies. Further, such people are ineligible for the benefits of 50 U.S.C. 22. The AG shall prepare a letter declaring this policy and transmit it to the Chief Justice of the United States, the chief judge of every circuit court of appeals, the chief judge of every district and territorial court of the United States, each Governor of a State and territory of the United States, and the highest-ranking judicial officer of each State and territory of the United States. The “Alien Enemies” described are subject to immediate apprehension, detention, and removal, and further that they shall not be permitted residence in the United States. Pursuant to the Alien Enemies Act, the AG the Secretary of DHS shall apprehend, restrain, secure, and remove every Alien Enemy described in this proclamation. Lastly, the proclamation describes various regulations that should be enacted to enforce this proclamation.

summaries.title: Achieving Efficiency Through State and Local Preparedness
summaries.aiSummary: This EO aims to give State and local governments and individuals a more active and significant role in national resilience and preparedness, streamline preparedness operations, and update government policies to reduce complexity. This includes establishing a new National Resilience Strategy, National Continuity Policy, National Critical Infrastructure Policy, and National Risk Register. DHS shall also proposed changes to the policies outlining the federal national framework.
