summaries.title: Removing Discrimination and Discriminatory Equity Ideology From the Foreign Service
summaries.aiSummary: The Secretary of State shall revise the 2022-2025 Decision Criteria for Tenure and Promotion in the Foreign Service, issued under section 2326.2 of title 3 of the Foreign Affairs Manual, to remove any reference to the Core Precept entitled “Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility.” The Secretaries shall promptly direct all employees of their Departments not to give this Core Precept any force or effect. Further, Secretaries shall direct all officers and employees of their Departments not to base Foreign Service recruitment, hiring, promotion, or retention decisions upon an individual’s race, color, religion, sex, or national origin; or while acting in an official capacity, promote, advocate for, or otherwise inculcate support for equity ideology. Secretaries shall take appropriate action if any current Foreign Service Members have knowingly and willfully engaged in unconstitutional or otherwise illegal discrimination based upon race or other protected characteristics.

summaries.title: Strengthening the Suitability and Fitness of the Federal Workforce
summaries.aiSummary: The OPM Director is delegated the authority to make final suitability determinations and take suitability actions regarding employees in the executive branch based on post-appointment conduct. A suitability action can include a directive by OPM to the head of an executive department or agency (agency) to remove an employee who does not meet the suitability criteria defined in OPM’s regulations. Further, the OPM Director shall propose regulations amending Part 731 of title 5, Code of Federal Regulations to reflect this. In drafting, the Director of OPM shall consider (1) requiring that an employing agency must make a referral to OPM in order for the Director of OPM to make a final suitability determination and take a suitability action regarding an employee based on post-appointment conduct, and (2) require agency compliance with OPM’s instructions within 5 days.

summaries.title: Stopping Waste, Fraud, and Abuse by Eliminating Information Silos
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs all Agency Heads to take all necessary steps to ensure Federal officials designated by the President or Agency Heads have full and prompt access to all unclassified agency records, data, software systems, and information technology systems for purposes of pursuing Administration priorities related to the identification and elimination of waste, fraud, and abuse. Further, agency heads should take all necessary steps to ensure the Federal Government has unfettered access to comprehensive data from all State programs that receive Federal funding. The Secretary of Labor shall receive unfettered access to all unemployment data and related payment records, including all such data and records currently available to the DOL Office of Inspector General.

summaries.title: Improving Education Outcomes by Empowering Parents, States, and Communities
summaries.aiSummary: The Secretary of Education shall take all necessary steps to facilitate the closure of the Department of Education and return authority over education to the States and local communities. The Secretary of Education shall ensure that the allocation of any Federal Department of Education funds is subject to rigorous compliance with Federal law and Administration policy, including the requirement that any program or activity receiving Federal assistance terminate illegal discrimination obscured under the label “diversity, equity, and inclusion” or similar terms and programs promoting gender ideology.

summaries.title: Eliminating Waste and Saving Taxpayer Dollars by Consolidating Procurement
summaries.aiSummary: This EO aims to consolidate federal procurement under GSA, rather than at individual agencies.

summaries.title: Immediate Measures To Increase American Mineral Production
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is imperative to national security to facilitate domestic mineral production to the maximum extent possible and directs various agency actions to do so. Further, special requirements are waived pursuant to the  national emergency declared in EO 14156, including  50 U.S.C. 4533(a)(1) through (a)(6);  50 U.S.C. 4531(d)(1)(a)(ii), 4332(d)(1)(B), and 4533(a)(1) through (a)(6).

summaries.title: Addressing Remedial Action by Paul Weiss
summaries.aiSummary: This EO revokes Executive Order 14237 of March 14, 2025 (Addressing Risks from Paul Weiss).

summaries.title: Preventing Abuses of the Legal System and the Federal Court
summaries.aiSummary: This Memo directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of DHS to prioritize enforcement of their respective regulations governing attorney conduct and discipline.  See, e.g., 8 C.F.R. 292.1 et seq.; 8 C.F.R. 1003.101 et seq.; 8 C.F.R. 1292.19. The AG shall take all appropriate action to refer for disciplinary action any attorney whose conduct in Federal court or before any component of the Federal Government appears to violate professional conduct rules. When the AG determines that conduct by an attorney or law firm in litigation against the Federal Government warrants seeking sanctions or other disciplinary action, the Attorney General shall recommend to the President any additional steps that may be taken, including reassessment of security clearances or termination of any Federal contract for which the relevant attorney or law firm has been hired. The AG shall review conduct by attorneys or their law firms in litigation against the Federal Government over the last 8 years and any misconduct that may warrant additional action shall be recommended to the President. AG shall periodically update the president on progress.

summaries.title: Rescinding Security Clearances and Access to Classified Information from Specified Individuals
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs agencies to take action to revoke security clearances for the following: Antony Blinken, Jacob Sullivan, Lisa Monaco, Mark Zaid, Norman Eisen, Letitia James, Alvin Bragg, Andrew Weissmann, Hillary Clinton, Elizabeth Cheney, Kamala Harris, Adam Kinzinger, Fiona Hill, Alexander Vindman, Joseph R. Biden Jr., and any other member of Joseph R. Biden Jr.’s family.

summaries.title: Greek Independence Day: A National Day of Celebration of Greek and American Democracy, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims March 25, 2025, as Greek Independence Day: A National Day of Celebration of Greek and American Democracy.

summaries.title: Imposing Tariffs on Countries Importing Venezuelan Oil
summaries.aiSummary: This EO finds that the actions and policies of the regime of Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela continues to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the US. On or after April 2, 2025, a tariff of 25 percent may be imposed on all goods imported into the US from any country that imports Venezuelan oil, whether directly from Venezuela or indirectly through third parties. Duties imposed by this order will be supplemental to duties on imports already imposed pursuant to IEEPA, section 232 of the Trade Expansion of 1962, section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, or any other authority. The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretaries of the Treasury, Commerce, DHS, and the United States Trade Representative, is hereby authorized to determine whether the tariff of 25 percent will be imposed on goods from any country that imports Venezuelan oil, directly or indirectly, on or after April 2, 2025. Once imposed on a country at the Secretary of State’s discretion, the tariff of 25 percent shall expire 1 year after the last date on which the country imported Venezuelan oil, or at an earlier date if the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretaries of State, Treasury, DHS, and the United States Trade Representative, so determines at his/her discretion.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks From Jenner & Block
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs a suspension pending review for any active security clearances held by individuals at Jenner & Block and a cessation of any government materials provided. Government contracting agencies shall, to the extent permissible by law, require Government contractors to disclose any business they do with Jenner & Block and whether that business is related to the subject of the Government contract. The heads of all agencies shall review all contracts with Jenner & Block or with entities that disclose doing business with it under subsection and take steps to terminate any contracts. The heads of all agencies shall provide guidance limiting official access from Federal Government buildings to employees of Jenner & Block when such access would threaten the national security of or otherwise be inconsistent with the interests of the United States and guidance limiting Government employees acting in their official capacity from engaging with Jenner & Block employees. Lastly, agency officials shall refrain from hiring employees of Jenner & Block, absent a waiver from the head of the agency, made in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

summaries.title: Immediate Declassification of Materials Related to the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Crossfire Hurricane Investigation
summaries.aiSummary: This memo states that all of the materials referenced in the Presidential Memorandum of January 19, 2021 (Declassification of Certain Materials Related to the FBI’s Crossfire Hurricane Investigation), are no longer classified. Further, the material proposed for redaction by the FBI in a cover letter dated January 17, 2021, remains classified. This does not extend to materials that must be protected from disclosure pursuant to orders of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court and does not require the disclosure of certain personally identifiable information.

summaries.title: Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account
summaries.aiSummary: This EO mandates the transition to electronic payments for all Federal disbursements and receipts by digitizing payments to the extent permissible under applicable law. Effective September 30, 2025, and to the extent permitted by law, the Secretary of the Treasury shall cease issuing paper checks for all Federal disbursements inclusive of intragovernmental payments, benefits payments, vendor payments, and tax refunds, except as specified in section 4 of this order. As soon as practicable, and to the extent permitted by law, all payments made to the Federal Government shall be processed electronically.

summaries.title: Protecting America's Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to promote financial integrity by enabling the Department of the Treasury to more easily conduct improper payment and fraud prevention screening prior to disbursing funds on behalf of agencies. Further, it aims to increase transparency and accountability by requiring agencies to provide the Department of the Treasury with the information needed to track transactions through the General Fund in greater detail.  This order also promotes operational efficiency by returning disbursing functions to the Department of the Treasury when possible and consolidating and standardizing core Federal financial systems.

summaries.title: Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to prohibit foreign nationals from voting in federal elections with documentary proof requirements.

summaries.title: Executive Grant of Clemency for Devon Archer
summaries.aiSummary: This EO grants a full pardon to Devon Archer.

summaries.title: Adjusting Imports of Automobiles and Automobile Parts into the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation finds that imports of automobiles and certain automobile parts continue to threaten to impair the national security of the United States. All imports of articles specified in Annex I to this proclamation or in any subsequent annex to this proclamation shall be subject to a 25 percent tariff with respect to goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after April 3, 2025, for automobiles, and on the date specified in the Federal Register for automobile parts, but no later than May 3, 2025. For automobiles that qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the USMCA, importers of such automobiles may submit documentation to the Secretary identifying the amount of U.S. content in each model imported into the United States.

summaries.title: Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History
summaries.aiSummary: This EO aims to update Smithsonian and National Zoo policies to remove programs that are inconsistent with federal law and policy, including those based on race or gender ideologies. Further, new members should be recruited to sit on the Smithsonian Board of Regents that will be committed to advancing the policy of this order.The Secretary of the Interior shall provide sufficient funding to improve the infrastructure of Independence National Historical Park, which shall be complete by July 4, 2026. Lastly, the Secretary of the Interior shall determine whether, since January 1, 2020, public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within the Department of the Interior’s jurisdiction have been removed or changed, and take action to reinstate the pre-existing monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties, as appropriate. Further, the Secretary of the Interior shall take action to ensure that all public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within its jurisdiction do not contain descriptions that inappropriately disparages Americans past or living.

summaries.title: Exclusions From Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs
summaries.aiSummary: This EO finds certain listed agencies and agency subdivisions to have as a primary function intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work and, therefore, Chapter 71 of title 5, United States Code, cannot be applied to these agencies. This EO also updates Executive Order 12171 of November 19, 1979 to add national security exclusions. Secretaries of Defense and Veterans Affairs are delegated authority under 5 U.S.C. 7103(b)(1) to issue orders suspending the application of section 1-402 or 1-404 of Executive Order 12171, as amended, to any subdivisions of the departments they supervise, thereby bringing such subdivisions under the coverage of the Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute. The Secretary of Transportation is delegated authority under section 7103(b) of title 5, United States Code, to issue orders excluding any subdivision of the Department of Transportation from Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute coverage or suspending any provision of that law with respect to any Department of Transportation installation or activity. With respect to employees in agencies or subdivisions thereof that were previously part of a bargaining unit but have been excepted under this order, each applicable agency head shall, upon termination of the applicable collective bargaining agreement: reassign any such employees who performed non-agency business pursuant to section 7131 of title 5 or section 4116 of title 22, United States Code, to performing solely agency business; and terminate agency participation in any pending grievance proceedings under section 7121 of title 5, United States Code, exceptions to arbitral awards under section 7122 of title 5, United States Code, or unfair labor practice proceedings under section 7118 of title 5 or section 4116 of title 22, United States Code, that involve such employees.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks From WilmerHale
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs a suspension pending review for any active security clearances held by individuals at WilmerHale and a cessation of any government materials provided. Government contracting agencies shall, to the extent permissible by law, require Government contractors to disclose any business they do with WilmerHale and whether that business is related to the subject of the Government contract. The heads of all agencies shall review all contracts with WilmerHale or with entities that disclose doing business with it under subsection and take steps to terminate any contracts. The heads of all agencies shall provide guidance limiting official access from Federal Government buildings to employees of WilmerHale when such access would threaten the national security of or otherwise be inconsistent with the interests of the United States and guidance limiting Government employees acting in their official capacity from engaging with WilmerHale employees. Lastly, agency officials shall refrain from hiring employees of WilmerHale, absent a waiver from the head of the agency, made in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

summaries.title: Making the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force to fight crime in DC and beautify the city.

summaries.title: Establishing the United States Investment Accelerator
summaries.aiSummary: Secretary of Commerce, in coordination with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, shall establish within the Department of Commerce an office named the United States Investment Accelerator (Investment Accelerator), which shall facilitate and accelerate investments above $1 billion in the United States by assisting investors as they navigate United States Government regulatory processes efficiently, reduce regulatory burdens, increase access to and use of our national resources, facilitate research collaborations with our national labs, and work with State governments to reduce regulatory barriers. The Investment Accelerator shall be responsible for the CHIPS Program.

summaries.title: Combating Unfair Practices in the Live Entertainment Market
summaries.aiSummary: Directs AG and FTC to ensure that competition laws are appropriately enforced in the concert and entertainment industry. The FTC and state Attorneys General shall rigorously enforce the Better Online Tickets Sales Act, 15 U.S.C. 45c. FTC shall take action, including new regulations and enforcement, to ensure price transparency and prevent unfair conduct in the secondary ticket market. Secretary of Treasury and AG shall ensure ticket scalpers are operating lawfully.

summaries.title: World Autism Awareness Day 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 2, 2025, as World Autism Awareness Day.

summaries.title: Further Amendment to Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China as Applied to Low-Value Imports
summaries.aiSummary: This EO imposes ad valorem and specific duties on low-value products (at or under $800) from PRC that would typically fall under the de minimis exception.

summaries.title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
summaries.aiSummary: An additional 10% ad valorem duty is imposed on all imports, with higher rates for certain countries as specified in Annex I. The 10% duty applies to imports starting April 5, 2025, with specific country rates from April 9, 2025. Certain goods, including steel, aluminum, automobiles and automobile parts, copper, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, lumber, certain critical minerals, and energy and energy products, are exempt (full list in Annex II). All good originating from Canada and Mexico that that do not qualify as originating under USMCA are subject to additional ad valorem duties of 25 percent, with energy or energy resources and potash imported from Canada and not qualifying as originating under USMCA presently subject to the lower additional ad valorem duty of 10 percent.

summaries.title: National Sexual Assault Awareness and Prevention Month, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 3, 2025 as National Sexual Assault Awareness and Prevention Month.

summaries.title: Cancer Control Month, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 2025 as Cancer Control Month.

summaries.title: National Donate Life Month, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 2025 as National Donate Life Month.

summaries.title: National Child Abuse Prevention Month, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 2025 as National Child Abuse Prevention Month.

summaries.title: Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summaries.aiSummary: This EO extends the enforcement delay specified in section 2(a) of Executive Order 14166 of January 20, 2025 (Application of Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act to TikTok), until June 19, 2025. The Attorney General shall further issue a letter to each provider stating that there has been no violation of the statute and that there is no liability for any conduct that occurred during the above-specified period,

summaries.title: Review of Proposed United States Steel Corporation Acquisition
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs CFIUS to conduct a review of the acquisition of U.S. Steel by the Purchasers to assist me in determining whether further action in this matter may be appropriate. The review shall specifically consider national security risks. Within 45 days, CFIUS shall submit a recommendation describing whether any measures proposed by the parties are sufficient to mitigate any national security risks identified by CFIUS.

summaries.title: Reinvigorating America's Beautiful Clean Coal Industry and Amending Executive Order 14241
summaries.aiSummary: The Chair of the National Energy Dominance Council (NEDC) shall designate coal as a “mineral” as defined in section 2 of Executive Order 14241 of March 20, 2025 (Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production), thereby entitling coal to all the benefits of a “mineral” under that order. Further, Executive Order 14241 is hereby amended by deleting the reference to “4332(d)(1)(B)” in section 6(d) of that order and replacing it with a reference to “4532(d)(1)(B)”. Agencies that are empowered to make loans, loan guarantees, grants, equity investments, or to conclude offtake agreements, both domestically and abroad, shall, to the extent permitted by law, take steps to rescind any policies or regulations seeking to or that actually discourage investment in coal production and coal-fired electricity generation. The Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, the United States Trade Representative, the Assistant to the President for National Security, and the heads of other relevant agencies, shall take all necessary and appropriate actions to promote and identify export opportunities for coal and coal technologies and facilitate international offtake agreements for United States coal. Secretaries of Energy and Interior shall determine whether coal/steel meets the definition of "critical material" under energy Act of 2020. The Secretary of Energy shall take all necessary actions, consistent with applicable law, to accelerate the development, deployment, and commercialization of coal technologies.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Promote American Energy
summaries.aiSummary: Proclaims that certain stationary sources subject to 89 FR 38508 are exempt from compliance for a period of 2 years beyond the Rule’s compliance date — i.e., for the period beginning July 8, 2027, and concluding July 8, 2029.  The effect of this Exemption is that, during this 2-year period, these stationary sources are subject to the compliance obligations that they are currently subject to under the MATS as the MATS existed prior to 89 FR 38508.

summaries.title: Amendment to Reciprocal Tariffs and Updated Duties as Applied to Low-Value Imports From the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: Increases HTSUS in Executive Order 14257 from 34% to 84% and de minimis tariff from 30% to 90%.

summaries.title: Strengthening the Reliability and Security of the United States Electric Grid
summaries.aiSummary: This EO empowers the Secretary of Energy to enhance the reliability and security of the U.S. electric grid during potential supply interruptions. It mandates expedited processes for grid operations and the development of a uniform methodology to analyze reserve margins. The order also establishes protocols for regularly assessing critical generation resources to ensure they remain available and prevent capacity reductions.

summaries.title: Protecting American Energy From State Overreach
summaries.aiSummary: AG is tasked with identifying and halting enforcement of state and local laws affecting domestic energy resources that may be unconstitutional or preempted by federal law, with a focus on those related to climate change and environmental initiatives. A report to the President detailing actions taken and recommendations for further measures is required within 60 days.

summaries.title: Education and Sharing Day, USA 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 9, 2025 as Education and Sharing Day, U.S.A.

summaries.title: Directing the Repeal of Unlawful Regulations
summaries.aiSummary: This memo orders agencies to take steps to repeal any regulation that exceeds its statutory authority, especially considering the listed court decisions (see memo for full list). This follows the review period ordered in Executive Order 14219.

summaries.title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates To Reflect Trading Partner Retaliation and Alignment
summaries.aiSummary: This EO modifies Executive Order 14257. First, it suspends from 4/10/25 - 7/9/25 country specific ad valorem rates, and instead enforces a 10% rate for all countries (except as otherwise provided). As of 4/10/25, the duty rate for Chinese products is increased to from 84% to 125% for HTSUS and from 90% to 120% for low value imports.

summaries.title: National Crime Victims' Rights Week, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 6-12, 2025 as National Crime Victims' Rights week.

summaries.title: Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting To Unleash American Energy
summaries.aiSummary: Directs the listed agencies and listed rules, where the agency is directed to issue a sunset rule effective no later than 9/30/25 in that covered regulation. The sunset provision shall provide that the agency will offer the public an opportunity to comment on the costs and benefits of each regulation prior to a rule’s expiration, and following such opportunity the Conditional Sunset Date for that Covered Regulation may be extended if the agency finds an extension is warranted.

summaries.title: Modernizing Defense Acquisitions and Spurring Innovation in the Defense Industrial Base
summaries.aiSummary: This executive order aims to accelerate U.S. defense procurement by reforming acquisition processes with a focus on speed, flexibility, and execution. It mandates a comprehensive review of existing acquisition process, internal regulations, acquisition workforce, Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System, and major defense acquisition programs.

summaries.title: Reforming Foreign Defense Sales To Improve Speed and Accountability
summaries.aiSummary: The phased implementation plan directs the Secretaries of State and Defense to promptly execute key actions, including implementing NSPM 10 of 2018, reevaluating missile technology restrictions, and engaging Congress to update notification processes for defense sales. Within 60 days, they will identify priority partners and end-items for arms transfers, ensuring these actions do not impair U.S. readiness and enhance allied burden-sharing. Annually, priority lists and munitions protections will be reviewed to focus on sensitive technologies. Plans to improve transparency and develop an electronic tracking system for defense sales will be submitted within 90 and 120 days, respectively.

summaries.title: National Former Prisoner of War Recognition Day, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 9, 2025 as National Former Prisoner of War Recognition Day.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks Associated with an Egregious Leaker and Disseminator of Falsehoods
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Attorney General, the Director of National Intelligence, and all other relevant agency heads to immediately take all action to suspend any active security clearances held by Miles Taylor, in addition to individuals at entities associated with Taylor, including the University of Pennsylvania, pending a review of whether such clearances are consistent with the national interest. Secretary of Homeland Security shall take all appropriate action to review Miles Taylor’s activities as a Government employee and submit a report.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks from Chris Krebs and Government Censorship
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Attorney General, the Director of National Intelligence, and all other relevant agency heads to immediately take all action to suspend any active security clearances held by Christopher Krebs, in addition to individuals at entities associated with Krebs, including SentinelOne pending a review of whether such clearances are consistent with the national interest. Secretary of Homeland Security shall take all appropriate action to review Kreb's activities as a Government employee and submit a report.

summaries.title: Restoring America's Maritime Dominance
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes a policy to revitalize and rebuild the domestic maritime industries and workforce, enhancing national security and economic prosperity. It mandates the creation of a Maritime Action Plan (MAP) to address legislative, regulatory, and fiscal aspects. Key actions include securing the maritime industrial base, addressing targeting by the PRC, enforcing cargo fees, engaging allies for aligned trade policies, incentivizing investment, launching a Maritime Security Trust Fund, and improving education and training in the maritime sector. The EO also calls for efficiency in procurement, expansion of the U.S. commercial fleet, securing Arctic waterways, and various deregulatory initiatives.

summaries.title: Reducing Anti-Competitive Regulatory Barriers
summaries.aiSummary: Agency heads, in consultation with the FTC Chairman and the Attorney General, are tasked with reviewing and identifying regulations that hinder market competition, including those that facilitate monopolies or create barriers to entry. Within 70 days, agencies must list such regulations and recommend whether they should be rescinded or modified. The FTC Chairman will gather public input through an RFI process and, after consolidating agency recommendations, will provide a list of anti-competitive regulations to the OMB Director for potential inclusion in the Unified Regulatory Agenda. This initiative aims to enhance market competition by removing unnecessary regulatory constraints.

summaries.title: Addressing Risks From Susman Godfrey
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs a suspension pending review for any active security clearances held by individuals at Susman and a cessation of any government materials provided. Government contracting agencies shall, to the extent permissible by law, require Government contractors to disclose any business they do with Susman and whether that business is related to the subject of the Government contract. The heads of all agencies shall review all contracts with Susman or with entities that disclose doing business with it under subsection and take steps to terminate any contracts. The heads of all agencies shall provide guidance limiting official access from Federal Government buildings to employees of Susman when such access would threaten the national security of or otherwise be inconsistent with the interests of the United States and guidance limiting Government employees acting in their official capacity from engaging with Susman employees. Lastly, agency officials shall refrain from hiring employees of Susman, absent a waiver from the head of the agency, made in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

summaries.title: Maintaining Acceptable Water Pressure in Showerheads
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Energy to publish in the Federal Register a notice rescinding Energy Conservation Program: Definition of Showerhead, 86 Fed. Reg. 71797 (December 20, 2021), including the definition of “showerhead” codified at 10 C.F.R. 430.2.  The rescission shall be effective 30 days from the date of publication of the notice, without a notice and comment period.

summaries.title: Clarification of Exceptions Under Executive Order 14257 of April 2, 2025, as Amended
summaries.aiSummary: This EO clarifies the exceptions set forth under EO 14247 as amended (4/2/25).

summaries.title: Military Mission for Sealing the Southern Border of the United States and Repelling Invasions
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Homeland Security to (1) provide for use and jurisdiction for DoD on federal lands; (2) provide for transfer and acceptance of jurisdiction over such Federal lands to enable military activities on military installation and for the designation of the federal lands as National Defense Areas by the Secretary of Defense. Secretary of Interior shall allow DoD use of Roosevelt Reservation not yet transferred/withdrawn.The Secretary of Defense may determine those military activities that are reasonably necessary and appropriate to accomplish the mission assigned in Executive Order 14167 and that are necessary to protect and maintain the security of military installations.

summaries.title: Ensuring Commercial, Cost-Effective Solutions in Federal Contracts
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal policy that agencies shall procure commercially available products and services, including those that can be modified to fill agencies’ needs, to the maximum extent practicable, including pursuant to the Federal Acquisition Streamlining Act of 1994 (Public Law 103-355, as amended) (FASA). Within 60 days, each agency shall review all open solicitations/notices where a commercial option has not been identified and evaluate whether a commercial option is available. 30 days later, each agency shall evaluate proposed action to advance commercial options. Within 120 days, and annually thereafter, each agency shall provide a report to OMB detailing the agency’s compliance with FASA and its progress toward implementing this order. Whenever an agency proposes to solicit a non-commercial product or service, the applicable contracting officer shall provide the specific reasons a non‑commercial product or service is required. The approval authority shall review and approve or deny the proposal in writing.

summaries.title: Updating Permitting Technology for the 21st Century
summaries.aiSummary: Directs agencies to adopt the maximum use of technology for environmental review and permitting for infrastructure projects. Within 45 days of the date of this memorandum, the Chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ), in consultation with the National Energy Dominance Council and relevant permitting agencies, shall issue a Permitting Technology Action Plan for modernizing the technology used for Federal permitting and environmental review processes for infrastructure projects. Within 90 days of issuance of the plan, the relevant officials should adopt and begin implementation of that plan. Within 15 days of the date of this memorandum, the Chairman of CEQ shall establish and lead an interagency Permitting Innovation Center that will design and test prototype tools that could be implemented pursuant to the Permitting Technology Action Plan for NEPA reviews and other environmental permits and authorizations.

summaries.title: Preventing Illegal Aliens from Obtaining Social Security Act Benefits
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Labor, the Secretary of HHS, and the Commissioner of Social Security, in consultation with the Secretary of DHS as necessary, shall take all reasonable measures to ensure ineligible aliens are not receiving funds from Social Security Act programs. The AG and the Commissioner of Social Security shall cooperate to detail and credential such Special Assistant United States Attorneys as are necessary to expand the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) full-time fraud prosecutor program to at least 50 United States Attorney Offices by October 1, 2025. Likewise, the AG and the Secretary of HHS shall cooperate to establish a similar fraud-prosecutor program utilizing Special Assistant United States Attorneys with regard to programs administered by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, which shall operate in at least 15 United States Attorney Offices by October 1, 2025. The Commissioner of Social Security shall (1)fully implement the recommendations in the Inspector General of the SSA’s Audit Report A-06-21-51022 and (2) shall refer promptly to the Inspector General of the SSA all earnings reports for persons age 100 or older when the purported wage-earner’s name does not match SSA’s files, and Inspector General of the SSA shall investigate such matters as appropriate. Within 60 days of the date of this memorandum, the Commissioner of Social Security shall review whether SSA should resume pursuing civil monetary penalties under section 1129 of the Social Security Act.

summaries.title: Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement
summaries.aiSummary: This EO aims to remove barriers for federal procurement and remove all FAR provisions not required by statute or essential to sound procurement. Within 180 days, the Administrator of the Office of Federal Public Procurement Policy (“Administrator”) shall take appropriate actions to amend the FAR to ensure that it contains only provisions that are required by statute or that are otherwise necessary to support simplicity and usability, strengthen the efficacy of the procurement system, or protect economic or national security interests. Within 15 days of the date of this order, each agency exercising procurement authority pursuant to the FAR shall designate a senior acquisition or procurement official to work with the Administrator and the FAR Council to ensure agency alignment with FAR reform and to provide recommendations regarding any agency-specific supplemental regulations to the FAR. The Administrator shall consider adding 4-year sunset provisions on the FAR provisions to be removed or reworked until this EO.

summaries.title: Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to optimize Federal health care programs, intellectual property protections, and safety regulations to provide access to prescription drugs at lower costs. The EO directs various agency actions to achieve this goal.

summaries.title: Ensuring National Security and Economic Resilience Through Section 232 Actions on Processed Critical Minerals and Derivative Products
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs a Section 232 investigation to determine the effects on national security of imports of processed critical minerals and their derivative products, including the impact on domestic production.

summaries.title: Restoring Common Sense to Federal Office Space Management
summaries.aiSummary: This EO revokes Executive Order 12072 and Executive Order 13006. The Administrator of General Services is directed to initiate the process to amend the regulations at title 41, parts 102-79 and 102-83, Code of Federal Regulations, and to take any other steps necessary to conform Federal office space management policy with this order. Agencies that acquire or utilize federally owned or leased space under authority other than the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (40 U.S.C. 101 et seq.), as amended, shall conform to the provisions of this order.

summaries.title: 250th Anniversary of the Battles of Lexington and Concord
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 19, 2025, as a day in commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the Battles of Lexington and Concord and the beginning of the American Revolutionary War.

summaries.title: Unleashing American Commercial Fishing in the Pacific
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation amends the management of the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument as initially set by Proclamation 9173, reverting to the management specifications of Proclamation 8336. Key points include the following: The Secretary of the Interior handles Monument Expansion management, while the Secretary of Commerce oversees fishery-related activities. Commercial fishing is allowed in specific zones, with only U.S.-flagged vessels permitted, except for certain transshipments. Military activities and national interests remain protected, and new rules to ease commercial fishing restrictions are to be proposed. Existing management remains unchanged unless stated.

summaries.title: Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to promote the productive harvest of US seafood resources; limit commercial fishing regulation; combat illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing; and protect seafood markets from the unfair trade practices of other nations. The Secretary of Commerce shall identify regulations to rescind or revise to further this goal, solicit public comments, and coordinate with various groups. Secretary of Commerce shall also coordinate with the Secretary of Interior to review national monuments to suggest opening them to commercial fishing.

summaries.title: Extension of Hiring Freeze
summaries.aiSummary: This memo extends the freeze on the hiring of Federal civilian employees within the executive branch as initially directed in the Presidential Memorandum of January 20, 2025 (Hiring Freeze). through July 15, 2025.

summaries.title: Honoring the Memory of His Holiness Pope Francis
summaries.aiSummary: Directs all federal US flags to be flown at half-staff in honor of Pope Francis on April 21, 2025.

summaries.title: White House Initiative To Promote Excellence and Innovation at Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the White House Initiative on Historically Black Colleges and Universities and the Department of Education the President’s Board of Advisors on Historically Black Colleges and Universities. These organizations will aim to foster opportunities, provide the highest quality education, obtain equal opportunities for federal programs, and ensure college-educated Americans are empowered. This EO also revokes EO 14041, White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity Through Historically Black Colleges and Universities.

summaries.title: Restoring Equality of Opportunity and Meritocracy
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to eliminate the “use of disparate-impact liability in all contexts to the maximum degree possible.” All agencies are directed to deprioritize enforcement of all statutes/regulations to the extent they include disparate-impact liability, including but not limited to 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2, 28 C.F.R.42.104(b)(2)–(3), 28 C.F.R. 42.104(b)(6)(ii), and 28 C.F.R. 42.104(c)(2). The DOJ shall review all statutes and regulations that include disparate-impact provisions. DOJ shall also determine if there are any situations where federal law can preempt state law for disparate-impact laws.

summaries.title: Reforming Accreditation To Strengthen Higher Education
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to reform accreditation for higher education. Specifically, the Secretary of Education is directed to monitor, investigate, and take appropriate action over higher education accreditation authorities, including those for medical and law schools, that violate federal law, including diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. Further, the Secretary of Education shall take steps to ensure accreditation prioritizes various ideas, including equal treatment and diverse thought.

summaries.title: National Volunteer Week, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 20-26, 2025 as National Volunteer Week.

summaries.title: National Park Week, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 19-27, 2025 as National Park Week.

summaries.title: Days of Remembrance of Victims of the Holocaust, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 20-27, 2025 as Days of Remembrance of Victims of the Holocaust.

summaries.title: Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to promote the appropriate integration of AI into education, including by providing training for educators. It also establishes a White House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Education and the Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge.

summaries.title: Preparing Americans for High-Paying Skilled Trade Jobs of the Future
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to optimize and target Federal investments in workforce development to align for skilled trades and other occupations, including Registered Apprenticeships.

summaries.title: Transparency Regarding Foreign Influence at American Universities
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Education to take all appropriate actions to enforce the requirements of section 1011f of title 20, United States Code to require complete and timely disclosure by higher education institutions of foreign funding. The Secretary of Education and other agencies shall take appropriate action to prospectively ensure that certification of compliance by higher education institutions with 20 U.S.C. 1011f and any other applicable foreign funding disclosure requirements is material for purposes of 31 U.S.C. 3729 and for receipt of appropriate Federal grant funds, which shall not be provided in cases of noncompliance with 20 U.S.C. 1011f and any other applicable foreign funding disclosure requirements.

summaries.title: Reinstating Commonsense School Discipline Policies
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Secretary of Education to take various actions to prevent “equity” ideology.

summaries.title: Strengthening Probationary Periods in the Federal Service
summaries.aiSummary: This EO amends the civil service rules to update the probationary and trial periods for federal employees. Further, the head of each agency shall make a list of all probationary employees and the agencies shall conduct performance reviews for all of these employees and determine whether to continue employment after the probationary period.

summaries.title: Investigation into Unlawful “Straw Donor” and Foreign Contributions in American Elections
summaries.aiSummary: This memo directs the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury to investigate allegations regarding the unlawful use of online fundraising platforms to make “straw” or “dummy” contributions or foreign contributions to political candidates and committees, and to take all appropriate actions to enforce the law.

summaries.title: Unleashing America's Offshore Critical Minerals and Resources
summaries.aiSummary: This EO aims to strengthen US leadership in seabed mineral exploration and development to address national security and economic challenges related to critical mineral supplies. This initiative involves enhancing domestic capabilities, fostering international partnerships, and streamlining permitting processes while ensuring environmental standards. Key actions include mapping seabed resources, supporting investment in relevant technologies, and collaborating with allies to counter foreign influence, particularly from China. The plan also emphasizes creating a robust domestic supply chain for these minerals to support economic growth and military preparedness.

summaries.title: World Intellectual Property Day, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims April 26, 2025 as World Intellectual Property Day.

summaries.title: Strengthening and Unleashing America's Law Enforcement To Pursue Criminals and Protect Innocent Citizens
summaries.aiSummary: The AG shall create a mechanism to provide legal resources and indemnification to law enforcement officers who unjustly incur expenses and liabilities for actions taken during the performance of their official duties to enforce the law (including private pro bono services). AG shall also take action to maximize federal resources to support state and local law enforcement resources. AG and DoD shall increase provisions of excess military and national security assets to state and local law enforcement. AG shall pursue all necessary legal remedies to ensure prosecution of people who obstruct the enforcement of criminal law and engage in civil rights violations, including those focused on diversity, equity, and inclusion.

summaries.title: Protecting American Communities From Criminal Aliens
summaries.aiSummary: This EO seeks to encourage immigration enforcement in “sanctuary jurisdictions.” Specifically, DOJ and DHS shall publish a list of state and local jurisdictions that obstruct federal immigration enforcement and enforce various consequences for those jurisdictions, including denial of federal funds or legal remedies. This EO also seeks to prevent federal benefits to aliens in “sanctuary jurisdictions.” Lastly, DOJ shall identify and take appropriate action to prevent enforcement of state and local laws that favor aliens over US citizens.

summaries.title: Enforcing Commonsense Rules of the Road for America's Truck Drivers
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs enforcement of an English language requirement to operate a commercial motor vehicle. Further, Secretary of Transportation shall review state commercial driver’s licenses to evaluate any irregularities and validate authenticity.

summaries.title: Addressing Certain Tariffs on Imported Articles
summaries.aiSummary: This EO updates prior tariff executive action so that the tariffs do not have a cumulative effect of “stacking” on one another.

summaries.title: Amendments to Adjusting Imports of Automobiles and Automobile Parts into the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation modifies proclamation 10908 by reducing duties assessed on automobile parts accounting for 15 percent of the value of an automobile assembled in the United States for 1 year and equivalent to 10 percent of that value for an additional year for automobile manufacturers meetings various requirements, including place of assembly and value.

summaries.title: 418th Anniversary of the First Landing and the Raising of the Cape Henry Cross
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims  April 29, 2025 as a day in celebration of the 418th anniversary of the First Landing and the Raising of the Cross at Cape Henry, Virginia, by the Jamestown settlers.

summaries.title: National Day of Prayer, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims May 1, 2025, as National Day of Prayer.

summaries.title: Loyalty Day and Law Day, U.S.A., 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims May 1, 2025, as Loyalty and Law Day.

summaries.title: National Fallen Firefighters Memorial Weekend, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims May 3-4, 2025, as National Fallen Firefighters Memorial Weekend.

summaries.title: Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Biased Media
summaries.aiSummary: Directs the CPB Board and all executive departments and agencies to cease Federal funding for NPR and PBS.

summaries.title: Establishment of the Religious Liberty Commission
summaries.aiSummary: This EO creates the Religious Liberty Commission to advise the White House Faith Office and the Domestic Policy Council on religious liberty policies of the United States.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief To Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order aims to strengthen the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain by removing regulatory barriers to domestic manufacturing. It directs the FDA, EPA, and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to review and streamline applicable regulations and guidance within 180 days to improve the timeliness and predictability of agency review processes. The order also calls for enhanced inspections of foreign pharmaceutical facilities, increased transparency on inspection activities, and centralized coordination of environmental permits for new manufacturing sites. The policy goal is to create a more resilient, competitive, and secure domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing base.

summaries.title: National Mental Health Awareness Month, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims May 2025 as National Mental Health Awareness Month.

summaries.title: National Hurricane Preparedness Week, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims May 4 through May 10, 2025, as National Hurricane Preparedness Week.

summaries.title: Improving the Safety and Security of Biological Research
summaries.aiSummary: This executive order directs various actions to ensure that United States federally funded research benefits American citizens without jeopardizing our Nation’s security, strength, or prosperity.  My Administration will balance the prevention of catastrophic consequences with maintaining readiness against biological threats and driving global leadership in biotechnology, biological countermeasures, biosecurity, and health research.

summaries.title: National Small Business Week, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This proclaims May 4 through May 10, 2025, as National Small Business Week.

summaries.title: Increasing Efficiency at the Office of the Federal Register
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs the Archivist of the United States, through the Office of the Federal Register, to improve the timeliness and cost-efficiency of publishing regulatory actions. It requires the Archivist to collaborate with the Government Publishing Office to modernize systems, reduce publication delays, and reassess the current fee schedule for publishing in the Federal Register. Reports on average publication times and cost adjustments must be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget at multiple intervals, with the goal of streamlining publication processes and aligning fees with actual costs.

summaries.title: Keeping Promises to Veterans and Establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to establish the National Center for Warrior Independence on the West Los Angeles VA campus to serve homeless veterans. The VA is tasked with developing a plan within 120 days to restore capacity to house up to 6,000 veterans by 2028. The order also requires coordination with other federal agencies to redirect applicable funds, expand housing and care access, and promote veteran self-sufficiency. Additional mandates include expanding healthcare options, conducting a feasibility study for a full-service VA medical center in New Hampshire, and improving overall service delivery through interagency cooperation. Accountability measures are also emphasized, with directives to address past personnel decisions and enhance oversight.

summaries.title: Establishing Project Homecoming
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation establishes "Project Homecoming," a federal initiative intended to encourage voluntary departure of individuals unlawfully present in the United States. The initiative directs the creation of technology-enabled return processes, including a government-funded return travel system and a financial incentive termed an “exit bonus.” It also sets penalties for those who choose not to depart, including increased immigration enforcement and potential legal and financial consequences.

summaries.title: Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs federal agencies to reduce reliance on criminal enforcement of regulatory violations, particularly those lacking clear mens rea (intent) requirements. Agencies are instructed to inventory and publicly disclose all criminally enforceable regulations within one year, update this list annually, and strongly discourage prosecution of offenses not included. Agencies must also revise future rulemakings to identify authorizing statutes and clearly state applicable mental state requirements. Within 45 days, each agency must publish guidance outlining factors to consider when referring violations for criminal prosecution. The order favors civil or administrative enforcement over strict liability criminal penalties and excludes immigration and national security-related enforcement from its scope.

summaries.title: Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order seeks to align U.S. prescription drug prices with those in comparably developed countries by implementing a “most-favored-nation” pricing strategy. It directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to communicate price targets to pharmaceutical manufacturers within 30 days and to facilitate direct-to-consumer programs offering drugs at the most-favored-nation price. If significant progress is not made, the order authorizes additional actions, including proposed rulemaking, importation certifications, antitrust enforcement, export controls, and potential FDA regulatory reviews. The order also calls on the Department of Commerce and USTR to address international pricing practices that contribute to disproportionately high drug costs for American consumers.

summaries.title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates To Reflect Discussions With the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order temporarily modifies certain tariffs imposed on imports from the People’s Republic of China (PRC), including Hong Kong and Macau, under prior Executive Orders related to trade imbalances and national security. Citing progress in trade discussions with the PRC, the President suspends a portion of the previously imposed tariffs for 90 days, lowering the ad valorem duty on specified imports from 34% or higher to 10%. The Order also reduces the tariff on certain low-value imports tied to the synthetic opioid supply chain from 120% to 54%, while maintaining a $100 duty per postal item. The modifications take effect May 14, 2025. Implementation is delegated to relevant agencies in coordination with the White House.

summaries.title: Restoring Gold Standard Science
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs federal agencies to adopt rigorous “Gold Standard Science” practices to restore public trust in the integrity of federally funded scientific research. Citing past misuse of scientific data, reproducibility concerns, and politicization of science, the order requires that scientific information used in policy decisions be transparent, reproducible, and objectively evaluated. Within 30 days, the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) must issue guidance outlining these standards, after which agencies must update their scientific integrity policies and report implementation actions within 60 days. Agencies are required to disclose influential data and models (with limited exceptions), communicate uncertainty and assumptions clearly, and apply a “weight of scientific evidence” approach in decision-making. Interim policies revert to those in place as of January 19, 2021, and actions taken between January 20, 2021, and January 20, 2025, must be reviewed for compliance. Each agency must also establish internal processes to address violations. The order applies to all employees and contractors involved in scientific activities, with limited waivers permitted by OMB and OSTP.

summaries.title: Reforming Nuclear Reactor Testing at the Department of Energy
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs the Department of Energy to accelerate the development, testing, and deployment of advanced nuclear reactors. It seeks to reform internal Department processes, streamline environmental reviews, and reduce regulatory delays that have hindered nuclear innovation. The Order requires the establishment of a pilot program to build at least three advanced reactors outside national laboratories by July 4, 2026, and mandates expedited timelines for application review and approval. It also instructs the Department to revise NEPA compliance procedures and coordinate with other federal offices to implement these reforms, aiming to restore U.S. leadership in nuclear energy innovation.

summaries.title: Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order establishes a comprehensive federal strategy to revitalize the United States’ nuclear energy sector in support of national security, energy independence, and technological leadership. It directs agencies to take actions aimed at strengthening the domestic nuclear fuel cycle, expanding uranium enrichment and conversion capacity, and improving the licensing and deployment of advanced reactors. The order also calls for the development of a long-term spent fuel management policy, repurposing decommissioned assets, and forming public-private agreements to secure nuclear fuel supplies. Additionally, it instructs federal agencies to support the restart and construction of nuclear plants, invest in advanced nuclear technologies, and prioritize nuclear-related workforce development through apprenticeships, education programs, and grant funding. The Department of Energy is tasked with leading many of these initiatives in coordination with other federal agencies, and all actions are to be implemented consistent with applicable law, budgetary requirements, and national security considerations.

summaries.title: Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs a comprehensive reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to streamline licensing, modernize regulations, and promote the deployment of advanced nuclear technologies. The order mandates structural and cultural changes at the NRC, including reorganization of staff and revisions to its regulatory framework to align with national energy and security priorities. It imposes fixed licensing deadlines, limits on fee recovery, encourages science-based radiation standards, and accelerates environmental reviews. These reforms aim to expand U.S. nuclear capacity, facilitate innovation, and enhance energy reliability and national security.

summaries.title: Deploying Advanced Nuclear Reactor Technologies for National Security
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs an accelerated federal effort to develop and deploy advanced nuclear reactor technologies to support U.S. national security, energy resilience, and global nuclear leadership. It mandates the use of nuclear power at defense and Department of Energy (DOE) sites, facilitates siting and fuel support for privately funded reactors, and strengthens interagency coordination. The order also promotes U.S. nuclear exports through expanded international agreements and financing strategies, and streamlines NEPA compliance. It seeks to enhance the domestic nuclear fuel cycle, ensure a long-term enriched uranium supply, and prioritize security clearances to support rapid deployment.

summaries.title: Adjusting Imports of Aluminum and Steel Into the United States
summaries.aiSummary: The proclamation raises national‑security tariffs on steel and aluminum (and their derivative articles) from 25 percent to 50 percent effective 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 4 2025; amends Executive Order 14289 so that articles already subject to Section 232 tariffs are not double‑assessed under other recent tariff programs; maintains the United Kingdom’s rate at 25 percent pending review under the May 8 2025 U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal; applies reciprocal‑tariff duties to any non‑steel/aluminum content; instructs U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to issue strict compliance guidance and penalties for misreporting steel or aluminum content; bars drawback on the new duties; and empowers the Secretary of Commerce—working with CBP and the U.S. International Trade Commission—to monitor imports, adjust UK tariff levels or quotas after July 9 2025, issue implementing regulations, and make any necessary Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTSUS) changes via the Federal Register.

summaries.title: Enhancing National Security by Addressing Risks at Harvard University
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation suspends the entry of foreign nationals who intend to study or participate in exchange programs at Harvard University under the F, M, or J visa categories, citing national security concerns and Harvard’s alleged noncompliance with federal information-sharing requirements. The proclamation outlines exceptions and allows for potential visa revocation for currently enrolled students. It also calls for a coordinated government response to enforce the suspension and evaluate whether it should be extended beyond its initial six-month duration.

summaries.title: Restricting the Entry of Foreign Nationals to Protect the United States from Foreign Terrorists and Other National Security and Public Safety Threats
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation by President Donald J. Trump, issued on June 4, 2025, imposes full or partial suspensions on the entry of immigrants and nonimmigrants from 19 countries due to inadequate identity-management, screening, and vetting capabilities. It builds on prior executive actions and emphasizes national security concerns, including terrorism, visa overstays, and non-cooperation in repatriation. The proclamation outlines exceptions, procedures for review and modification, and implementation measures, and it directs relevant agencies to regularly assess and engage with affected countries.

summaries.title: Restoring American Airspace Sovereignty
summaries.aiSummary: The Executive Order creates a whole‑of‑government push to secure U.S. airspace against malicious or careless drone use. It establishes a National Security Council‑led task force, directs the FAA to speed new flight‑restriction rules and publish open geofencing data, empowers DOJ and DHS to enforce and fund counter‑UAS measures for state and local partners, mandates inter‑agency upgrades to drone‑detection guidance and data‑sharing, and lays groundwork for a national Counter‑UAS training center—all on rapid timelines that prioritize critical infrastructure, mass gatherings, and border security.

summaries.title: Leading the World in Supersonic Flight
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order launches a federal push to revive commercial supersonic flight over land. It directs the Federal Aviation Administration to lift decades‑old bans, set interim and permanent noise standards, and modernize related rules; instructs the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy to coordinate R&D across multiple agencies; and tasks the Departments of Transportation and State with building international consensus and safety agreements so U.S.‑made supersonic aircraft can operate globally.

summaries.title: Unleashing American Drone Dominance
summaries.aiSummary: The order launches a government‑wide initiative to make the United States the world leader in commercial drones and advanced air‑mobility (eVTOL) aircraft. It directs the FAA to fast‑track rules for beyond‑visual‑line‑of‑sight (BVLOS) flights, deploy AI to speed waiver approvals, and run a nationwide eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. It also mandates an updated UAS integration roadmap, ramps up test‑range use, tightens supply‑chain security with a Covered Foreign Entity List, accelerates trusted U.S. drone exports, and compels the Defense Department to scale domestic drones for training and combat—all on aggressive deadlines.

summaries.title: Eliminating Waste, Fraud, and Abuse in Medicaid
summaries.aiSummary: This memorandum directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to take immediate steps to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse in the Medicaid program, particularly by ending state-directed payment schemes that inflate Medicaid reimbursements far above Medicare levels. The President orders alignment of Medicaid payment rates with Medicare, where legally permissible, to protect the program’s financial sustainability and ensure fairness across federal healthcare systems.

summaries.title: Sustaining Select Efforts To Strengthen the Nation's Cybersecurity and Amending Executive Order 13694 and Executive Order 14144
summaries.aiSummary: This order rewrites and tightens Executive Order 14144 on national‑cybersecurity innovation, adds quantum‑resilience and AI‑security mandates, and revises the cyber‑sanctions framework in EO 13694. It sets firm deadlines for NIST, CISA, NSA, OMB and others to update secure‑software and patching standards, publish post‑quantum product lists, make research data sets public, embed AI‑vulnerability management, pilot machine‑readable “rules‑as‑code,” and launch a Federal purchasing rule that requires the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark on IoT products—while instructing OMB to overhaul Federal cyber‑risk guidance within three years.

summaries.title: Department of Defense Security for the Protection of Department of Homeland Security Functions
summaries.aiSummary: The memorandum orders the Secretary of Defense to federalize at least 2,000 National Guard troops for up to 60 days (plus any needed active‑duty forces) to protect ICE personnel, other Federal officers, and immigration‑related Federal property where violent protests threaten operations; the Secretary must coordinate the call‑up with State governors and the National Guard Bureau, ensure forces perform only necessary protective missions, and consult the Attorney General and Secretary of Homeland Security before any withdrawal.

summaries.title: Presidential Permit Authorizing Green Corridors, LLC, to Construct, Maintain, and Operate a Commercial Elevated Guideway Border Crossing Near Laredo, Texas, at the International Boundary Between the United States and Mexico
summaries.aiSummary: This Presidential Memoranda grants Green Corridors, LLC a Presidential Permit to construct, operate, and maintain a commercial elevated guideway and border-crossing facility at the U.S.–Mexico border in Laredo, Texas. The permit is subject to strict conditions, including regulatory compliance, environmental mitigation, interagency coordination, facility funding commitments, inspection requirements, and bilateral authorization through diplomatic channels. The permit expires if construction does not begin within five years.

summaries.title: Stopping Radical Environmentalism to Generate Power for the Columbia River Basin
summaries.aiSummary: This Presidential Memorandum revokes the September 27, 2023, memorandum that prioritized ecological restoration in the Columbia River Basin—specifically efforts to breach dams for fish protection. It directs the withdrawal from the associated litigation MOU, rescinds the 2024 environmental review process, and requires Federal agencies to reassess and report on actions, commitments, and funding tied to the previous administration's policy.

summaries.title: Empowering Commonsense Wildfire Prevention and Response
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order responds to the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires by directing Federal agencies to streamline wildland fire governance, enhance local preparedness and response, modernize prevention tools, and remove regulatory barriers. It prioritizes interagency cooperation, incentivizes local action, promotes innovative technology and land management practices, and calls for performance metrics and regulatory review to improve efficiency and effectiveness in combating wildfires.

summaries.title: Presidential Permit Authorizing the City of Laredo, Texas, to Expand and Continue to Maintain, and Operate a Vehicular Border Crossing at the Laredo-Colombia Solidarity International Bridge Land Port of Entry
summaries.aiSummary: This memoranda grants the City of Laredo a Presidential Permit to expand and continue operating the Laredo-Colombia Solidarity International Bridge Land Port of Entry, including the construction of two new commercial traffic spans. The permit outlines conditions for regulatory compliance, interagency coordination, environmental protection, inspection facilities, diplomatic authorization, and federal oversight. The permit will expire if construction has not commenced within five years.

summaries.title: Implementing the General Terms of the United States of America-United Kingdom Economic Prosperity Deal
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order implements provisions of the U.S.–U.K. Economic Prosperity Deal, facilitating enhanced market access, tariff modifications, and structured trade quotas to bolster U.S. national security and economic interests. It establishes tariff-rate quotas for U.K. automotive imports, lifts tariffs on certain aerospace products, and sets the stage for future quotas on steel and aluminum imports from the U.K., contingent on compliance with supply chain security and national interest considerations.

summaries.title: Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order further extends the enforcement delay of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (Public Law 118-50) as it pertains to TikTok, until September 17, 2025. During this time, the Department of Justice (DOJ) is prohibited from taking enforcement action or imposing penalties under the Act. The order also directs the Attorney General to issue guidance and notifications affirming non-liability for any conduct during the delay period and to defend the Executive Branch’s exclusive enforcement authority under the Act.

summaries.title: Presidential Permit Authorizing the City of Eagle Pass, Texas, to Expand and Continue to Maintain and Operate a Vehicular and Pedestrian Border Crossing at the Camino Real International Bridge Land Port of Entry
summaries.aiSummary: Grants the City of Eagle Pass, Texas, a Presidential Permit to expand and continue operating the Camino Real International Bridge Land Port of Entry. The expansion includes a second bridge span with six additional vehicle lanes. The permit sets forth conditions related to legal compliance, environmental protections, federal coordination, inspection facilities, and construction authorization. The permit will expire in five years if construction has not begun.

summaries.title: Text of a Letter from the President to the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate
summaries.aiSummary: On June 21, 2025, U.S. forces, under the President’s direction, conducted a limited, precision strike on three Iranian nuclear weapons development facilities. The action was taken to protect vital U.S. national interests and in collective self-defense of Israel. No ground troops were used, and the operation was designed to minimize casualties and avoid escalation. The President justified the strike under his constitutional authority as Commander in Chief and stated it was consistent with international law. This report is submitted to Congress under the War Powers Resolution.

summaries.title: Saving College Sports
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order aims to stabilize and preserve college athletics in the United States by protecting non-revenue and women’s sports, prohibiting third-party pay-for-play arrangements, and clarifying the legal status of student-athletes. It directs federal agencies to use regulatory, funding, enforcement, and litigation tools to ensure fair treatment of athletes and preserve the educational and developmental benefits of collegiate sports. The order also calls for safeguards to ensure the continued contribution of college sports to the development of Olympic athletes.

summaries.title: Providing for the Revocation of Syria Sanctions
summaries.aiSummary: This EO recalibrates U-S sanctions policy toward Syria in light of political changes under President Ahmed al-Sharaa. It ends the 2004 Syria national emergency and broad, economy-wide sanctions, yet strengthens and modernizes targeted measures against former Assad-era officials, human-rights violators, captagon traffickers, and obstructionists to Syria’s political transition. It directs the Departments of State, Treasury, and Commerce to use waiver, reporting, and regulatory authorities under the Caesar Act, the Syria Accountability Act, and the Chemical and Biological Weapons Act; to consider selective sanctions relief; to pursue new counter-terrorism designations; and to advance U-S goals at the United Nations—all while ensuring no benefit flows to terrorist groups or proliferators.

summaries.title: Simplifying the Funding of Energy Infrastructure and Critical Mineral and Material Projects
summaries.aiSummary: The memorandum directs federal agencies to coordinate more closely when funding energy-infrastructure and critical-mineral projects. Agencies must share application and award data with the National Energy Dominance Council (NEDC), pause new obligations if applicants refuse to allow that sharing, revise their own rules to facilitate it, and work with the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to create a single, government-wide funding application that applicants can submit once for multiple programs. The goal is to cut duplicative reviews, speed decisions, and strengthen domestic energy and critical-mineral supply chains.

summaries.title: PRESIDENTIAL PERMIT AUTHORIZING SOUTH BOW (USA) LP TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN PIPELINE FACILITIES AT CAVALIER COUNTY, NORTH DAKOTA, AT THE INTERNATIONAL BOUNDARY BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA
summaries.aiSummary: Grants a Presidential Permit to South Bow (USA) LP to operate and maintain existing cross-border pipeline facilities located in Cavalier County, North Dakota. The permit covers the transport of all hydrocarbon and petroleum products (excluding natural gas regulated under the Natural Gas Act) between the U.S. and Canada. It supersedes a 2020 permit and sets forth compliance requirements regarding safety, ownership, inspection, reporting, indemnification, and national security access.

summaries.title: AUTHORIZING JUNCTION PIPELINE COMPANY, LLC TO CONSTRUCT, CONNECT, OPERATE, AND MAINTAIN PIPELINE FACILITIES AT TOOLE COUNTY, MONTANA, AT THE INTERNATIONAL BOUNDARY BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA
summaries.aiSummary: Grants Junction Pipeline Company, LLC a Presidential Permit to construct, connect, operate, and maintain cross-border pipeline facilities in Toole County, Montana, for the import of crude oil and other petroleum products from Canada to the United States. The permit outlines conditions for regulatory compliance, inspection, national security access, environmental responsibility, reporting obligations, and procedures for termination or transfer of ownership. The permit is subject to all applicable U.S. laws and does not cover natural gas regulated under the Natural Gas Act.

summaries.title: Establishing a White House Office for Special Peace Missions
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order establishes a new White House Office for Special Peace Missions, headed by a Presidentially-appointed Special Envoy, charged with coordinating U.S. efforts to end conflicts abroad in partnership with the Department of State, Department of Defense, and other relevant agencies.
