It preserves existing departmental authorities, affirms budgetary and legal constraints, and clarifies that the Order creates no enforceable private rights.

summaries.title: PRESIDENTIAL PERMIT AUTHORIZING STEEL REEF US PIPELINES LLC TO OPERATE AND MAINTAIN PIPELINE FACILITIES AT BURKE COUNTY, NORTH DAKOTA, AT THE INTERNATIONAL BOUNDARY BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA
summaries.aiSummary: Grants Steel Reef US Pipelines LLC a Presidential Permit to continue operating and maintaining existing cross-border pipeline facilities in Burke County, North Dakota, for the export of natural gas liquids to Canada. The permit imposes requirements related to operational standards, regulatory compliance, federal oversight, reporting, and future changes in ownership or use. It also grants the U.S. Government the authority to take temporary possession of the facilities in the interest of national security and outlines procedures for termination or transfer of the permit.

summaries.title: National Security Presidential Memorandum/NSPM-5
summaries.aiSummary: The memorandum amends and re-issues National Security Presidential Memorandum-5 to tighten U.S. restrictions on dealings with Cuba’s government and security services while expanding support for the Cuban people. It orders a suite of regulatory changes, reporting requirements, audits, and interagency reviews to ensure that U.S. travel, finance, and engagement benefit Cuba’s private sector and civil society rather than the Cuban military or intelligence services, and directs annual assessments of progress toward democratic transition and human-rights improvements.

summaries.title: Establishing the President's Make America Beautiful Again Commission
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order establishes the President’s Make America Beautiful Again Commission to coordinate conservation and access efforts across federal land management agencies. The order emphasizes restoring public access to federal lands, streamlining environmental management, supporting voluntary conservation, and promoting outdoor recreation. It directs interagency collaboration on issues like wildlife recovery, clean water access, and infrastructure repair in national parks and forests, with an overarching goal to preserve America's outdoor heritage for future generations.

summaries.title: Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs the Department of the Interior to revise pricing, access, and infrastructure policies for national parks and related lands. The goal is to increase revenue from foreign visitors, enhance affordability and access for U.S. residents, reduce maintenance backlogs, and encourage broader domestic and international use of underutilized parks. The order revokes a 2017 memorandum on diversity and inclusion and calls for agency rule reviews to align with the current administration's recreational access policy.

summaries.title: Ending Market Distorting Subsidies for Unreliable, Foreign-Controlled Energy Sources
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs the Department of the Treasury and the Department of the Interior to implement provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that eliminate tax credits and federal support for wind, solar, and other “green” energy sources. It emphasizes ending preferential treatment for such projects, tightening construction eligibility criteria, and enforcing restrictions related to foreign-controlled supply chains. Reports detailing agency actions and findings must be submitted to the President within 45 days.

summaries.title: Extending the Modification of the Reciprocal Tariff Rates
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order extends until August 1, 2025, the temporary suspension of increased reciprocal tariffs originally imposed under Executive Order 14257. The extension applies to most U.S. trading partners, excluding China, whose tariff treatment remains governed by a separate order. The order modifies the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTSUS) accordingly and authorizes relevant agencies to implement the changes using authorities granted under IEEPA and other applicable laws.

summaries.title: Ensuring Accountability and Prioritizing Public Safety in Federal Hiring
summaries.aiSummary: This Presidential Memorandum imposes a temporary freeze on hiring for Federal civilian positions within the Executive Branch through October 15, 2025. It prohibits filling vacant or creating new positions unless explicitly exempted, consistent with the Merit Hiring Plan issued by OPM. The order allows for limited exceptions—such as for national security, public safety, and legally required services—and outlines a process for departmental approval and OPM notification. It prohibits the use of external contracting to bypass the freeze and encourages internal staff reallocation to support agency priorities and maintain essential services.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Promote American Security with Respect to Sterile Medical Equipment
summaries.aiSummary: The President has exempted the commercial sterilization facilities listed in Annex I from complying with the EPA’s April 5, 2024 Ethylene Oxide (“EtO”) emissions rule for two years beyond each original deadline—on the grounds that required control technologies are not yet commercially viable and that maintaining EtO sterilization capacity is critical to patient care and national security.

summaries.title: Creating Schedule G in the Excepted Service
summaries.aiSummary: The order establishes a new “Schedule G” in the excepted service to cover noncareer positions of a policy-making or policy-advocating character that customarily turn over with each Presidential administration. It amends Civil Service Rule VI (5 CFR 6.2 and 6.4) to list Schedule G alongside existing excepted‐service schedules (A, B, C, D, E and Policy/Career) and to clarify that most civil‐service removal rules do not apply to positions in these schedules. The Director of OPM is directed to issue implementing regulations (with particular focus on 5 CFR part 213), and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs is instructed, when filling Schedule G posts, to ensure appointees embody the President’s policies without regard to political affiliation or activity. The order affirms it does not create enforceable private rights and is subject to available appropriations.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Promote American Chemical Manufacturing Security
summaries.aiSummary: The President has exempted the facilities listed in Annex I from complying with the EPA’s March 6, 2024 Taconite Rule for an additional two years beyond each original deadline, on the grounds that required emissions‐control technology is not yet commercially available and that maintaining domestic taconite processing is critical to national security and supply‐chain resilience.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Further Promote American Energy
summaries.aiSummary: The President has exempted the coal-fired units listed in Annex I from the EPA’s May 7, 2024 Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) revision for two years beyond the Rule’s July 8, 2027 compliance date—i.e. until July 8, 2029—on the grounds that requisite emissions-control technologies are not yet commercially viable and that preserving reliable, affordable power is critical to national security and grid resilience.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Promote American Iron Ore Processing Security
summaries.aiSummary: The President has exempted the facilities listed in Annex I from complying with the EPA’s March 6, 2024 Taconite Rule for an additional two years beyond each original deadline, on the grounds that required emissions‐control technology is not yet commercially available and that maintaining domestic taconite processing is critical to national security and supply‐chain resilience.

summaries.title: Promoting the Export of the American AI Technology Stack
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order establishes a national initiative—the American AI Exports Program—to promote the global deployment of U.S.-origin full-stack artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. It directs the Department of Commerce to solicit and evaluate industry proposals for AI export packages and, in coordination with other federal agencies, to support selected projects with financing tools, regulatory assistance, and diplomatic engagement. The initiative aims to bolster U.S. technological leadership and reduce foreign dependence on adversarial AI technologies.

summaries.title: Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order promotes the rapid development of large-scale data centers and supporting infrastructure crucial to artificial intelligence and national security by streamlining permitting, utilizing federal lands, and coordinating agency support. It defines qualifying projects based on size, national security relevance, or designation by key federal departments. The order revokes EO 14141 and instructs agencies to ease regulatory burdens, accelerate environmental reviews, and identify funding or land access to expedite such projects.

summaries.title: Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order directs federal agencies to ensure that large language models (LLMs) procured by the government are developed in accordance with two principles: truth-seeking and ideological neutrality. It asserts that models should not prioritize ideological agendas—specifically criticizing diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) frameworks—at the expense of factual accuracy or neutrality. The order requires the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), in consultation with relevant offices, to issue guidance on how agencies should implement these principles in procurement and contracting.

summaries.title: Ending Crime and Disorder on America's Streets
summaries.aiSummary: This Executive Order establishes a new federal policy approach toward homelessness, emphasizing public safety and the use of civil commitment and institutional treatment for individuals with serious mental illness or substance use disorders. It directs federal agencies to reassess grant priorities, discourage harm-reduction models, and enforce stricter standards for program participation and accountability. The order also aims to redirect funding toward programs that reduce homelessness and crime, while enhancing data-sharing with law enforcement and expanding requirements for housing programs.

summaries.title: Suspending Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries
summaries.aiSummary: This EO ends the duty-free de minimis exemption provided under 19 U.S.C. 1321(a)(2)(C) for any shipment of articles not covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), regardless of value, country of origin, mode of transportation, or method of entry.  Further, all such shipments, except those sent through the international postal network, shall be subject to all applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges. International postal shipments not covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b) shall be subject to the duty rates described in this order.

summaries.title: Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of Brazil
summaries.aiSummary: This EO declares a national emergency and imposes an additional ad valorem duty rate of 40% on certain products of Brazil.

summaries.title: President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition, and the Reestablishment of the Presidential Fitness Test
summaries.aiSummary: This EO revokes EO 13824 (2018) and amends EO 13265 (2002). This EO reestablishes the Presidential Fitness Test and establishes the President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition to advise on progress of this order.

summaries.title: Further Modifying the Reciprocal Tariff Rates
summaries.aiSummary: This EO declares that the national emergency declared in EO 14257 remains and that additional ad valorem duties on goods of certain trading partners are required. Annex I of this EO includes the specific countries, rates, and goods subject to the additional duties.

summaries.title: Amendment to Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
summaries.aiSummary: This EO declares that the emergency declared in Executive Order 14193 remains and that the additional ad valorem rate of duty of 25% for products of Canada shall increase to 35%.

summaries.title: Establishing the White House Task Force on the 2028 Summer Olympics
summaries.aiSummary: This EO creates the White House Task Force on the 2028 Summer Olympics, which is responsible for coordinating, assisting, and planning various aspects of the games.

summaries.title: Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of the Russian Federation
summaries.aiSummary: This EO finds that the national emergency declared in EO 14066 continues and that Russia continues to pose a threat to the US. As such, an additional 25% ad valorem rate of duty is applied to India 21 days after this EO. The Secretary of Commerce and any other relevant heads of agencies shall determine whether other countries are importing (directly or indirectly) Russian oil and further determine whether an additional 25% ad valorem rate of duty should be imposed.

summaries.title: Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking
summaries.aiSummary: This EO requires federal agencies to implement stricter review processes for discretionary grants, specifically prohibiting grants for activities that promote racial preferences, deny "binary" sex, facilitate illegal immigration, or any other initiative against public safety or American values. Agencies must designate senior officials to oversee grantmaking, prioritize accountability, streamline application requirements, and include terms allowing termination of grants that no longer align with agency priorities or the national interest.

summaries.title: Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the Department of Labor and other federal regulators to reevaluate and clarify guidance to allow fiduciaries of 401(k) and other defined-contribution retirement plans to prudently include alternative assets—such as private equity, real estate, and digital assets—in participant investment options.

summaries.title: Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal banking regulators to eliminate guidance and practices that enable financial institutions to restrict access to banking services based on a customer's political or religious beliefs, or lawful business activities, instead requiring decisions be based on neutral, risk-based criteria. Further, it mandates remedial actions for past violations, including reinstatement of affected clients, disciplinary measures against institutions engaging in "politicized or unlawful debanking," and development of a comprehensive strategy to prevent such conduct going forward.

summaries.title: Declaring a Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia
summaries.aiSummary: This EO declares a public safety emergency in the District of Columbia due to rising violent crime and directs the Mayor to provide the services of the Metropolitan Police Department for federal purposes, with operational control delegated to the Attorney General. The Attorney General is tasked with monitoring the situation, consulting with appropriate officials, and regularly updating the President.

summaries.title: Further Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates To Reflect Ongoing Discussions With the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This EO states that it is necessary and appropriate to continue the suspension effectuated by Executive Order 14298 until 12:01 a.m. on November 10, 2025.

summaries.title: Enabling Competition in the Commercial Space Industry
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to streamline and expedite regulatory processes—including environmental reviews, licensing, and permitting—for commercial space launches, reentry operations, and spaceport infrastructure, aiming to make the United States a leader in space innovation and industry by 2030. It also mandates interagency coordination, regulatory reform, and enhanced leadership roles to bolster American competitiveness in novel space activities while maintaining national security priorities.

summaries.title: Ensuring American Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Resilience by Filling the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs HHS to identify approximately 26 critical drugs and ensure a six-month supply of their active pharmaceutical ingredients —preferably sourced domestically—is stockpiled in the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR). Additionally, it requires an updated plan to maintain reserves for essential medicines, including opening a second SAPIR repository, to bolster supply chain resilience against future public health emergencies.

summaries.title: Revocation of Executive Order on Competition
summaries.aiSummary: This EO revokes EO 14036 (Promoting Competition in the American Economy) originally issued on July 9, 2021.

summaries.title: Improving Our Nation Through Better Design
summaries.aiSummary: The executive order establishes the “America by Design” initiative and a National Design Studio to modernize and improve the usability and aesthetics of federal digital and physical services, led by a newly created Chief Design Officer. Agencies are required to collaborate with the Chief Design Officer to prioritize and implement design enhancements, with initial results due by July 4, 2026, while ensuring compliance with existing laws and regulations.

summaries.title: Measures To End Cashless Bail and Enforce the Law in the District of Columbia
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to take all lawful steps to halt cashless bail policies in Washington, D.C., prioritizing the pretrial detention of criminal suspects who pose a threat to public safety and encouraging federally-supported charges and custody whenever possible. Additionally, it instructs the Attorney General and executive departments to review existing police and judicial practices, and to use available administrative and budgetary actions to press D.C. to restore cash bail for offenders considered dangerous.

summaries.title: Prosecuting Burning of the American Flag
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to prioritize enforcement of laws against acts of American Flag desecration that incite violence or violate existing content-neutral statutes, consistent with First Amendment limits. It also authorizes immigration-related penalties for foreign nationals involved in flag desecration and encourages federal coordination with state and local authorities for further action.

summaries.title: Additional Measures To Address the Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs multiple federal agencies to take immediate measures to address public safety and disorder in the District of Columbia, including hiring additional law enforcement personnel, forming specialized units, and increasing oversight of housing and transit conditions. It also authorizes increased cooperation and resource allocation for rapid response to civil disturbances and mandates review of police practices to ensure the effective mitigation of the crime emergency.

summaries.title: Taking Steps To End Cashless Bail To Protect Americans
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to identify and potentially suspend or terminate federal funding to states and local jurisdictions that have substantially eliminated cash bail for defendants charged with serious crimes. It establishes a policy that federal resources should not support jurisdictions with cashless bail practices, in order to promote public safety and ensure pretrial detention of individuals who pose a risk to society.

summaries.title: Further Exclusions From the Federal Labor- Management Relations Program
summaries.aiSummary: This EO expands national security exclusions under federal labor-management relations law by designating additional agencies and agency subdivisions as primarily engaged in intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work, thus exempting them from Chapter 71 of Title 5. It also amends prior executive orders to add new excluded units and provides an expedited timeline for implementing related determinations by the Secretaries of Defense and Veterans Affairs.

summaries.title: Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes that classical and traditional architectural styles are the preferred designs for major Federal public buildings, emphasizing their capacity to inspire civic virtue, connect citizens to the nation’s founding ideals, and visually distinguish government properties. It directs GSA to prioritize these styles in planning, design competitions, and selection processes, and requires additional scrutiny and presidential notification when alternative architectural styles are proposed.

summaries.title: Implementing the United States-Japan Agreement
summaries.aiSummary: This EO implements a new United States–Japan trade agreement by establishing a baseline 15 percent tariff on nearly all Japanese imports, with sector-specific exceptions and significant market access openings for American producers, alongside Japan’s commitment to invest $550 billion in the United States. It authorizes the Secretary of Commerce and other relevant officials to adjust, monitor, and enforce these tariff measures and related regulations.

summaries.title: Strengthening Efforts To Protect U.S. Nationals From Wrongful Detention Abroad
summaries.aiSummary: This EO empowers the Secretary of State to designate foreign governments as "State Sponsors of Wrongful Detention" if they engage in or support the wrongful detention of U.S. nationals, triggering a range of retaliatory actions such as sanctions, travel restrictions, assistance limits, and export controls. It also outlines criteria for termination of such designations and extends these measures to entities controlling territory.

summaries.title: Restoring the United States Department of War
summaries.aiSummary: This EO authorizes the DoD to adopt the secondary title "Department of War" and "Secretary of War" in official and ceremonial contexts. It directs the Secretary of Defense to report on initial implementation and recommend steps for a permanent name change, while clarifying that statutory references and legal authorities remain unchanged pending further legislative action.

summaries.title: Modifying the Scope of Reciprocal Tariffs and Establishing Procedures for Implementing Trade and Security Agreements
summaries.aiSummary: The EO revises tariff exemptions for certain goods in response to ongoing national security and trade deficit concerns, authorizing modifications to tariff schedules and the implementation of trade agreements with aligned foreign partners. It empowers relevant agencies to update duties, monitor trade practices, and negotiate future tariff adjustments to advance U.S. national economic and security interests.

summaries.title: Restoring Law and Order in Memphis
summaries.aiSummary: The President has established a Memphis Safe Task Force composed of federal, state, and local agencies to combat the city's high rates of violent crime through coordinated law enforcement, aggressive prosecution, and increased presence in affected neighborhoods. Additionally, the President has authorized the mobilization of Tennessee National Guard units to support public safety and Task Force operations, with ongoing assessment of whether further executive action is needed to restore law and order in Memphis.

summaries.title: Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summaries.aiSummary: This EO further extends the delay of enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act against TikTok and similar entities until December 16, 2025, prohibiting the DOJ from taking any action or imposing penalties for noncompliance during this period or for related conduct prior to the order. Additionally, it directs the Attorney General to issue guidance and confirmation of non-liability for affected providers, while asserting the Executive's exclusive authority over enforcement of the Act.

summaries.title: Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between the Long Island Rail Road Company and Certain of Its Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations
summaries.aiSummary: This EO creates an emergency board, effective September 18, 2025, to investigate and report on unresolved labor disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and its employees represented by specified unions, with the board's report due within 30 days. For 120 days after its establishment, no changes to the conditions related to the disputes will be made except by agreement, and the board will terminate upon submission of its report.

summaries.title: The Gold Card
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the "Gold Card" visa program, which allows individuals or corporate sponsors who make a significant unrestricted financial gift to the Department of Commerce ($1 million for individuals, $2 million for corporations) to be eligible for expedited immigrant visas based on exceptional business ability and national benefit. The Secretaries of Commerce, State, and Homeland Security are directed to implement and administer this program within 90 days, including guidelines for application, expedited adjudication, status transfer, and fund usage to promote commerce and American industry.

summaries.title: Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigration Workers
summaries.aiSummary: This presidential proclamation restricts entry of new H-1B workers unless employers pay a $100,000 fee, imposes stricter compliance measures, and calls for higher prevailing wage levels.

summaries.title: Designating Antifa as a Domestic Terrorist Organization
summaries.aiSummary: This executive order designates Antifa as a domestic terrorist organization. It directs all relevant executive departments and agencies to use their authorities to investigate, disrupt, and dismantle illegal Antifa operations, consistent with applicable law.

summaries.title: Countering Domestic Terrorism and Organized Political Violence
summaries.aiSummary: The President has directed federal agencies to implement a comprehensive strategy to disrupt and dismantle organized domestic terrorist networks responsible for political violence, including targeted intimidation, doxing, and attacks on federal officers and facilities. This strategy includes increased investigation, prosecution, financial tracking, and potential designation of domestic terrorist organizations, making the prevention of politically motivated terrorism a national law enforcement priority.

summaries.title: Enforcing the Death Penalty Laws in the District of Columbia to Deter and Punish the Most Heinous Crimes
summaries.aiSummary: The President has directed federal prosecutors to fully enforce the death penalty in the District of Columbia, making it a priority for crimes warranting capital punishment, especially in light of recent public safety concerns in the nation's capital. The memorandum instructs the Attorney General and the U.S. Attorney for D.C. to seek the death penalty in all appropriate cases, ensuring robust implementation of federal capital punishment laws.

summaries.title: Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security
summaries.aiSummary: This EO determines that TikTok’s proposed divestiture of its U.S. operations meets the requirements to resolve national security concerns under the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act. It also directs the Attorney General to pause enforcement of the Act for 120 days to allow the divestiture to be completed, and establishes ongoing federal oversight to ensure compliance and security safeguards.

summaries.title: Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
summaries.aiSummary: This EO extends the operation of numerous federal advisory committees, task forces, and councils until September 30, 2027, assigning responsibility for each committee to the relevant department or agency. It also updates previous executive orders and specifies that appointed department heads are to perform functions required under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for these committees.

summaries.title: Assuring the Security of the State of Qatar
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes that the United States will consider any armed attack against Qatar as a threat to its own peace and security, committing to take all necessary measures to defend Qatar and restore stability. The order further mandates ongoing joint contingency planning and diplomatic cooperation to guarantee Qatar’s territorial integrity and support its role in mediation and conflict resolution.

summaries.title: Unlocking Cures for Pediatric Cancer With Artificial Intelligence
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to harness artificial intelligence to accelerate pediatric cancer research, improve data sharing, and enhance clinical care, prioritizing innovation, investment, and interoperability in health data. It establishes a coordinated effort to use AI-enabled solutions for better diagnostics, treatments, and prevention, while ensuring patient privacy and encouraging public and private sector engagement.

summaries.title: Department of War Security for the Protection of Federal Personnel and Property in Illinois
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation creates authorization to mobilize at least 300 members of the Illinois National Guard for up to 60 days to protect federal property and personnel. This order remains in effect until the Governor of Illinois consents to a federally funded mobilization and directs the Secretary of War to coordinate with state and federal officials, ensuring the Guard performs all necessary protective measures to uphold federal law.

summaries.title: Construction of Arctic Security Cutters
summaries.aiSummary: The President has directed the phased construction of up to four Arctic Security Cutters in foreign shipyards due to urgent national security needs in the Arctic, while requiring a plan to develop domestic expertise for future icebreaker builds. This is a temporary measure to address capability gaps and does not preclude continued investment in the U.S. shipbuilding industrial base, with authorization expiring in four years unless extended.

summaries.title: The Trump Declaration for Enduring Peace and Prosperity
summaries.aiSummary: The undersigned welcome the Trump Peace Agreement as a historic step toward ending conflict in Gaza and fostering enduring peace, security, and prosperity for both Palestinians and Israelis, with respect for all faith communities and their heritage. They commit to resolving future disputes diplomatically, combating extremism, and collaboratively building a region grounded in mutual respect, opportunity, and peaceful coexistence.

summaries.title: National Security Presidential Memorandum/NSPM-8
summaries.aiSummary: Due to a prolonged lapse in congressional appropriations, the President has authorized the Secretary of War and the Director of the OMB to use any available Department of War funds to ensure continued payment of military personnel, safeguarding military readiness and national security. Once the appropriations lapse ends, funding accounts should be adjusted as permitted by law to maintain ongoing Department of War operations and activities in line with pre-lapse expenditure plans.

summaries.title: Ensuring Continued Accountability in Federal Hiring
summaries.aiSummary: This EO freezes most federal civilian hiring except for specified priority roles and requires agencies to establish Strategic Hiring Committees and submit annual staffing plans to ensure efficiency and alignment with administration priorities. It outlines specific exceptions and exemptions, mandates regular reporting, and reaffirms that its provisions will not impair essential services or conflict with applicable law.

summaries.title: Adjusting Imports of Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles , Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicle Parts, and Buses into the United States
summaries.aiSummary: This proclamation found that rising imports of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, vehicle parts, and buses threaten U.S. national security by undermining domestic supply chains critical to defense, emergency response, and infrastructure. In response, the President has imposed new tariffs and established offset programs to strengthen domestic manufacturing, safeguard supply chains, and maintain U.S. control over essential vehicle and part production.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Promote American Mineral Security
summaries.aiSummary: Proclaims that copper is essential to U.S. energy, defense, and manufacturing. As such, the President has issued a 2-year exemption from new EPA requirements for certain smelters, citing the lack of available technology and the critical importance of maintaining domestic mineral processing capacity for national security.

summaries.title: Modifying Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This EO orders the reduction of additional tariffs on certain Chinese goods from 20 percent to 10 percent, effective November 10, 2025, while continuing to monitor China's compliance with these measures. The Secretary of Homeland Security and other officials will oversee implementation, and further action may be taken if China fails to meet its obligations under this agreement.

summaries.title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates Consistent With the Economic and Trade Arrangement Between the United States and the People's Republic of China
summaries.aiSummary: This EO suspends heightened reciprocal tariffs on imports from China until November 10, 2026. This arrangement is intended to help reduce the U.S. trade deficit, strengthen national security and economic interests, and will be monitored for compliance, with the option for further action should China fail to meet its commitments.

summaries.title: Fostering the Future for American Children and Families
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs federal agencies to modernize the foster care system through improved technology, data collection, and partnerships, while expanding resources and opportunities for youth transitioning out of foster care. It also seeks to remove barriers for qualified foster and adoptive parents, especially those with sincerely held religious beliefs, and encourages collaboration with faith-based organizations to support families and children in need.

summaries.title: Modifying the Scope of the Reciprocal Tariffs With Respect to Certain Agricultural Products
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs that certain agricultural products be exempted from reciprocal tariffs previously imposed to address national security concerns arising from persistent U.S. goods trade deficits, effective November 13, 2025, with corresponding updates to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule and refund procedures. Relevant officials will continue to monitor the situation and have authority to take further action as necessary, while all departments are directed to implement these changes in accordance with applicable law.

summaries.title: Modifying the Scope of Tariffs on the Government of Brazil
summaries.aiSummary: This EO exempts certain Brazilian agricultural products from previously imposed tariffs due to initial progress in bilateral negotiations, while directing federal agencies to implement and monitor these changes.

summaries.title: Regulatory Relief for Certain Stationary Sources to Promote American Coke Oven Processing Security
summaries.aiSummary: This grants a two-year exemption from certain compliance requirements of the EPA’s Coke Oven Rule for specified stationary sources, citing the lack of commercially viable technology and the importance of coke production to national security, infrastructure, and defense. During this period, affected facilities must comply with the pre-existing standards rather than the new rule’s requirements and deadlines.

summaries.title: Designation of Certain Muslim Brotherhood Chapters as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists
summaries.aiSummary: This executive order directs U.S. agencies to consider designating certain chapters of the Muslim Brotherhood, particularly those in Lebanon, Jordan, and Egypt, as foreign terrorist organizations and specially designated global terrorists, based on their violent activities and threats to U.S. interests and partners, and requires federal action toward these designations within specified timeframes.

summaries.title: Launching the Genesis Mission
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes the “Genesis Mission,” a national initiative led by the Department of Energy to accelerate scientific discovery and technological innovation through an integrated AI platform that leverages federal research resources, datasets, and partnerships, aiming to advance key science and technology challenges, strengthen national security, and maintain U.S. global leadership in AI.

summaries.title: Aligning United States Core Childhood Vaccine Recommendations with Best Practices from Peer, Developed Countries
summaries.aiSummary: This memorandum directs federal health officials to review childhood vaccine recommendations from peer, developed countries and update U.S. guidelines if superior, evidence-based practices are identified, while maintaining access to all currently available vaccines.

summaries.title: Addressing Security Risks from Price Fixing and Anti-Competitive Behavior in the Food Supply Chain
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes Food Supply Chain Security Task Forces within the Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission to investigate and address anti-competitive behavior, especially by foreign-controlled companies, in U.S. food supply chains, and requires joint briefings to congressional leaders at 180 and 365 days regarding progress and recommended legislative actions.

summaries.title: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
summaries.aiSummary: This EO stablishes a national policy framework to promote U.S. dominance in artificial intelligence by minimizing state regulations, particularly those that hinder innovation or compel ideological bias in AI models. It directs the creation of a federal AI Litigation Task Force to challenge inconsistent state laws, restricts certain federal funding to states with onerous AI regulations, and initiates proceedings to potentially preempt conflicting state laws through federal standards. The order also calls for legislative recommendations to solidify a uniform federal approach, while preserving state authority over areas like child safety, infrastructure, and procurement.

summaries.title: Protecting American Investors From Foreign-Owned and Politically-Motivated Proxy Advisors
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs increased federal oversight and regulation of proxy advisory firms, citing concerns that their guidance to shareholders is politicized and may compromise investor returns. The order instructs the SEC, FTC, and DOL to consider revising related regulations, enhance transparency, investigate anticompetitive and deceptive practices, and strengthen fiduciary standards to ensure proxy advisors act solely in clients' financial interests. Its aim is to restore public confidence in the industry by prioritizing investor protection, accountability, and competition.

summaries.title: Designating Fentanyl as a Weapon of Mass Destruction
summaries.aiSummary: This EO designates illicit fentanyl and its precursor chemicals as Weapons of Mass Destruction due to their extreme lethality and use by criminal organizations threatening U.S. national security. It directs federal agencies to strengthen investigations, prosecutions, sanctions, interagency cooperation, and military preparedness against the fentanyl threat. The order mandates a unified and elevated federal response to disrupt fentanyl trafficking and bolster homeland defense against potential large-scale chemical attacks involving fentanyl.

summaries.title: Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay
summaries.aiSummary: This EO sets new pay rates and salary schedules for federal employees across various statutory pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, and certain executive, legislative, and judicial positions, effective January 1, 2026. It also adjusts pay for uniformed services and authorizes the Director of the OPM to consider an additional increase for certain law enforcement personnel, and establishes new locality-based comparability payments. The order supersedes the previous pay adjustment order from December 2024.

summaries.title: Ensuring American Space Superiority
summaries.aiSummary: This EO sets a comprehensive national space policy focused on returning Americans to the Moon by 2028, establishing a permanent lunar outpost, enhancing missile and space security, growing the commercial space economy, and advancing space technology such as nuclear power for lunar missions. It requires federal agencies to reform acquisition processes, strengthen international partnerships, and implement strategies for space security and spectrum leadership, while prioritizing commercial solutions and efficient operations. The order supersedes prior space policy directives and aligns all federal efforts with these new space exploration, security, and economic priorities.

summaries.title: Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025
summaries.aiSummary: This EO closes all federal departments and agencies, excusing employees from duty on December 24 and December 26, 2025, except for those required for national security, defense, or public need. It ensures that these dates are treated as federal holidays for pay and leave purposes. OPM is directed to take necessary actions to implement this order.

summaries.title: Increasing Medical Marijuana and Cannabidiol Research
summaries.aiSummary: This EO directs the expedited rescheduling of marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, acknowledging its accepted medical use and reduced abuse potential. It further calls for a regulatory framework and improved research on both medical marijuana and hemp-derived CBD products, including clear guidance on THC limits and accurate product labeling. The order aims to close gaps in medical knowledge so patients and providers may access safe, effective, and well-informed treatment options.

summaries.title: Regarding the Acquisition of Certain Assets of Emcore Corporation by Hiefo Corporation
summaries.aiSummary: This EO finds credible evidence that HieFo Corporation—controlled by a citizen of the People’s Republic of China—may threaten U.S. national security through its completed April 30, 2024 acquisition of EMCORE’s digital chip and related wafer design/fabrication/processing assets, and asserts other laws are insufficient to address the risk. It therefore prohibits the transaction and any ongoing HieFo ownership, requires divestment within 180 days (subject to CFIUS extension), and imposes interim access, transfer, reporting, and audit/verification controls enforced and overseen by CFIUS.

summaries.title: Prioritizing the Warfighter in Defense Contracting
summaries.aiSummary: This EO declares a policy to accelerate defense procurement by curbing major defense contractors’ stock buybacks and dividends when they are underperforming, failing to invest in production capacity, or not prioritizing U.S. Government contracts. It directs the Secretary of War to identify such contractors, require remediation plans, and—if issues persist—use available legal and contractual enforcement tools and add future contract clauses restricting buybacks/dividends and tying executive compensation to on-time delivery and increased production rather than short-term financial metrics.

summaries.title: Safeguarding Venezuelan Oil Revenue for the Good of the American and Venezuelan People
summaries.aiSummary: This EO declares a national emergency and uses IEEPA/NEA authority to protect certain U.S.-held Venezuela-related funds from attachment or other judicial process, citing U.S. national security and foreign policy interests in Venezuelan stability. It defines “Foreign Government Deposit Funds,” makes any attachment or similar process null and void, restricts any transfer or dealing absent Treasury authorization, and directs Treasury (with State/DOJ) to hold the funds in a custodial sovereign capacity and assert sovereign immunity in proceedings.

summaries.title: Establishing a Second Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between the Long Island Rail Road Company and Certain of Its Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations
summaries.aiSummary: This EO establishes a second Presidential Emergency Board under § 9A of the Railway Labor Act to investigate and resolve ongoing labor disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and employees represented by five unions. It requires final settlement offers within 30 days, directs the Board to choose the most reasonable offer and report to the President within the next 30 days, and mandates a status quo period (no unilateral changes) until 60 days after the Board’s report.

summaries.title: Stopping Wall Street From Competing With Main Street Homebuyers
summaries.aiSummary: This EO sets a policy that large institutional investors should not buy single-family homes that could otherwise be purchased by families. It directs Treasury to define key terms, requires major housing-related agencies to issue guidance limiting federal facilitation or disposition of homes to such investors (with narrow build-to-rent exceptions), increases antitrust and disclosure scrutiny of investor acquisitions and rental practices, and calls for legislation to codify the policy.
